We can make use of the **Five Pillars of Healthy Hormones** and apply them toward healing our gastrointestinal tract. Those Pillars are summarized as follows: we are going to balance your hypothalamus, get your nutrition in balance, make sure you get adequate exercise, restorative sleep and a healing mindset. All very important because this affects your gut health. Let us begin with the first Two Pillars.
topics: The Five Pillars of Healthy Hormones

sections.module_title: Your Gastrointestinal Tract and Hormonal Balance
sections.title: Pillars One and Two: Balance Your Gut’s Brain with Healthy Nutrition
sections.text:
We must bring balance to your gut brain, and for this task I have found much success with **Genesis Gold** for many of my patients with imbalances. Genesis Gold is designed to balance your **hypothalamus** and soothe your **neuroendocrine system**. This can be quite effective for digestion problems as the two systems are so interlinked. I have observed irritable bowel syndrome, both the diarrhea-related irritable bowel syndrome as well as the constipation variety of irritable bowel syndrome, solved using Genesis Gold. Such a treatment still leaves us to put your bacteria in balance, and we still must heal the lining of the gut. However, without addressing the communicative effects between your gut and brain, your GI tract will go back to an imbalanced state. This is especially true for cases of irritable bowel syndrome. Your lower gut remembers that it is an anxious bowel with diarrhea, or that it is a depressed bowel with slow **peristalsis** and constipation. Peristalsis is an involuntary constriction and relaxation of the muscles of the intestine. This must be addressed before progress can be made.

*[Image: a jar of Genesis Gold with its green powder.]*

So we also use Genesis Gold because it is rich in digestive aids, probiotics, prebiotics, as well as rich in a variety of vital nutrients for healthy bacterial flora. These vital nutrients can otherwise be obtained by eating a large variety of colorful vegetables and fruits, as Genesis Gold duplicates the **microbial diversifying** effects of a **healthy diet**. Therefore, Genesis Gold is the first step to balancing the hypothalamus and the gut. Healing foods for a healthy gut. But you may remember that I called for getting rid of foods?

So we must start you off with a **bland elimination diet**, which means you are not eating much variety, so we can identify the offending irritating food to which you are sensitive. Identifying that food will require trial and retrial, and food histories may be necessary to know what is going on. While this testing is ongoing, a bland diet will soothe your inflamed gut. By eating plain white rice or, more specifically, drinking the starchy water from preparing white rice can work wonders to heal your gut. I have observed cases of severe diarrhea in pediatric patients, or even pets, in which drinking the water pulled from starchy white rice did quite a job of healing their diarrhea within six to eight hours. Therefore, there is something to be said for foods normally avoided in an insulin resistant diet, as they are often quite healing.

*[Image: a basket of vegetables — greens, cabbage, broccoli, carrots, sweet potatoes, lotus root, mushrooms, asparagus, bean sprouts (plant-rich nutrition for gut health).]*

Be sure that you are not reintroducing foods to your system that are irritating, such as **spicy foods**. Nor should you start with **cruciferous vegetables or legumes**, as they can cause gas. You must wait two to three days to reintroduce a new food. This is because it may take two to three days to get each reintroduced food though your system and to record your body’s reaction to that food. Once you eliminate everything suspect or complex, it may take a period of **six to eight weeks to truly flush out your system**. After that cleansing is accomplished, you may reintroduce each new food over a two to three day period. That will allow us to determine if your body is ready for that food, and there may be some backtracking. For example, if a patient were to be reacting to citrus, we would remove it from their system for at least six weeks, before reintroducing citrus for a period of two to three days. If the patient’s body does not react, then they are most likely not affected by citrus. It will then be time to add corn or such higher in fat foods, like red meat, back into the diet, depending on what the body is reacting to.

> **Exercise: You are What You Eat**
> - Before you see a Healthcare Professional about your GI Tract, Make a Diet Journal
> - Note the general food groups in each of your meals
> - Notice imbalances with the Food Pyramid
> - Bring your Journal to your Medical appointment, so both of you can narrow down your food sensitivity.

Let us take a moment to discuss the GAPS diet. The **GAPS diet** was developed in the UK and is principally focused on gut immunity. It is a program that aids the body in healing autoimmunity issues and is very strict. GAPS is one of the diets which my patients tend to struggle to maintain, but the diet is definitely worth the struggle, especially if we cannot easily ascertain what is irritating your gut. This is because the GAPS diet gives us a strict regimen in testing your sensitivity to foods and food reintroduction.

There is also the **Low FOD-MAPS diet**. This diet focuses on fermentable poorly absorbed starches and sugars, the primary suspects in food reactions. You can observe the principles of this diet when you experience flatulence and gassy bloating from beans, as that fermentable sugar and starch in the bean is causing the gas. We call those specific sugar-starches FOD-MAPS, they are found in many different foods. So, eating foods that are lower in fermentable sugars will help with gas and bloating. I encourage you to explore [Low FOD-MAPS](https://stanfordhealthcare.org/medical-treatments/l/low-fodmap-diet.html) and [GAPS](http://www.gapsdiet.com/) diets to see what they entail. I do not recommend very strict diets, but if a patient’s gut is really unhealthy (meaning they have a variety of gut issues, such as gas, or if they are experiencing rectal bleeding due to inflamed intestine) then a strict diet is called for and these two diets are where we start.

sections.text:
*[Image: a group doing yoga on a beach (physical activity for gut health).]*

What activity is healing for a healthier gut? Well, your gastrointestinal tract needs you to be **active**, so if you are sitting or lying down often, you must massage your gut with movements of the abdominal muscles, which help to move food through your system. You must be active to have a healthy gut, you must walk around, do some kind of activity, for the good of your gut. That said, sometimes unusually aerobic or stringent aerobic activity can cause more irritation in an already irritable bowel. It is imperative that you find the **right balance of activity** for your gut. Restorative exercises, such as yoga and pilates, help you lower your cortisol stress hormones, which helps your gut heal. Even in such cases as a patient coming out of surgery, when their digestion is sluggish from anesthetics, getting the patient out of bed and having them walk is necessary to get their gut moving. This assists the body in passing gas, gets bowel movements going, so that they can start eating again. **Walking** is incredibly healing to the gut.

But what about **restorative sleep** for a healthy gut? That’s important too! If you are not getting an adequate amount of sleep, your body cannot heal that gut lining. Remember, most healing occurs when we are sleepy or asleep. So you need to sleep, in complete **darkness**, and you need to get at least **seven to eight hours** of sleep a night. Observe the comparative sleeping positions in the image to the right. You will see a person lying on their right side and because of the way your stomach and your gut is aligned, right side sleeping is more likely to cause heartburn within the esophagus. That stomach acid will creep into the throat, causing irritation. Even sinus inflammation is sensitive to which side of the body you sleep on, **sleeping on your left side** is a healthier anatomical position to keep your stomach acids where they belong.

> **[Graphic]** Slide "4) Restorative sleep for a healthy gut": get an adequate amount of sleep in the dark to heal the gut lining and restore normal function. Illustration: lying on the right side lets gastric juice flow back toward the esophagus, while lying on the left side keeps gastric juice in the stomach (left-side sleeping helps reflux).

A **healing mindset** is essential for a healthy gut. Studies have shown that irritable bowel syndrome is absolutely associated with anxiety and depression. As previously discussed here, you can manipulate the brain’s chemistry through the actions of the bowel. Often times, I find, people with irritable bowel syndrome will have issues in their childhood that cause hypersensitivity **to normal sensations** of digestion, such as hunger, bowel movements, or the routine passage of food through the GI tract. My patients have become hypersensitized to these sensations and so healthy activity induces a **stress response**. We definitely can be sure that there is a relationship between the psychological and the physiological, thus I have found that psychological and spiritual healing makes a huge difference in treating irritable bowel syndrome.

> **[Graphic]** Slide "5) Healing mindset for a healthy gut" — emotional links Deborah teaches: IBS with anxiety and depression; gallbladder disease with worry; constipation with suppressing emotion; diarrhea with anxiety; malabsorption with unworthiness.

We also have associated anxiety to gallbladder disease, in which patients suffer **cholecystitis**, meaning their gallbladder is so inflamed that ingesting fat causes gallbladder pain or even sedimentary buildup, these patients often tend to be worried. I have observed this relationship between the gallbladder and worrying. For such patients, it would not matter if their gallbladder were removed, if they still suffer **anxiety**, then their bile ducts will suffer from the production of too much acid and not enough bile salts. This can lead to issues with clogged bile ducts in the liver.

Comparatively, I find that **constipation** is usually related to **suppressing your emotions**. People who are very emotive also tend to hold on to the stool in their bowels. People that are anxious tend to get **diarrhea**, we have explored that causal relationship. How many times have you experienced anxiety with your heart racing, and you also felt urgency for an immediate bowel movement? That occurs because the same neurotransmitters that are responsible for mental experiences of anxiety also increase peristalsis in your gut. I find that patients with malabsorption also tend to have a “poor me” kind of attitude of unworthiness. It is almost as if they feel unworthy of their own nutrition, unworthy of the ability to keep themselves healthy. If we do not heal the mind and the mindset, we will be treating a patient’s gut issues forever.

As you can see, a multipronged approach can heal all of the pillars of your health. Your hypothalamus, your nutrition, your activity level, your sleep and your mindset are needed to heal your gut. You can also keep your gut healthy with [Genesis Gold](https://genesisgold.com/genesisgold/).

> **[Graphic]** Closing slide: "Keep your gut healthy with Genesis Gold®" — www.genesisgold.com.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.text:
Greetings, I am Deborah Maragopoulos, Intuitive Integrative Nurse Practitioner. This document is focused on fitness, obesity and our metabolism. One of the key phrases that I use for these topics is “fit or fat”. When my children were growing up, my personal experience with weight issues and eating disorders led to the word “fat” being an “F word” in our house. We often talked about whether a person was “fit or not fit”.

While we are going to be using the word “fat” to talk about body fat percentages, please understand that fitness is more important than weight. We will also focus on body composition and how our genes affect our hunger and our weight. Our hunger hormones also play a role and so we are also going to focus on what we can do to control all this.

sections.module_title: Fitness, Obesity, and the Healthy Metabolism
sections.title: Measuring Fitness Instead of Weight
sections.text:
But, first, please understand that weight is a huge issue for most people. Most people are focused, especially women but men as well, on how much they weigh rather than how **fit** they are (which is to say how much body fat they have). Women, for instance, do not accrue their full bone mass until they are over 30. So, if a woman is really focused on lowering her weight to 115 pounds, like she did when she was 20 years old, then when she is 40 years old she will be disappointed. There is no way she can go back to that state without losing lean body mass, because she probably gained anywhere from 5 to 10 pounds of bone mass between the ages of twenty and thirty-five.

So, it is very important to not focus on your weight, but to instead focus on how much fat you have on your body. That factor is a lot more important to your hormonal health and your fitness. The image to the right is a **General Body Fat Percentage** range, note that everyone has essential fat. You may also notice that women need a lot more essential fat on their bodies than men do, and this fat is needed to produce hormones. Men only need two percent to five percent, while women need ten percent to thirteen percent. Athletes typically carry a lower percentage of body fat — 14–20% for women and 6–13% for men — though they can weigh more because of their muscle.

> **[Graphic]** Table "General body fat percentages" — Women / Men: essential fat 10–13% / 2–5%; athletes 14–20% / 6–13%; fitness 21–24% / 14–17%; acceptable 25–31% / 18–24%; at risk 32%+ / 25%+. Beside it: BMI, body-fat %, lean body mass — body fitness reflects cellular health (vital capacity and cellular respiration).

> **Measuring Fitness, instead of Fat Exercise:**
> - Can you define the difference between BF, LBM, and BMI?
> - Using what you have learned, what is your body fat index?
> - What category are you in?

If you are a woman, you are fit if you are in the 21% to 24% fat to body weight. If you are a man, 14% to 17% fat to body weight is considered fit. Notice the wide difference between males and females and what is considered normal body fat for each. We consider the 25% to 31% range acceptable for females and, for men the 18% to 24% range is considered acceptable. Now “acceptable” means that you are not at risk for disease due to your percentage of body fat. However, once women are over 32%, or men are over 25%, the risk increases for metabolic diseases, such as diabetes or heart disease. Therefore, it is important that we pay attention to our body fat percentage. So, BMI which is the very first little marker here is body mass index. That doesn’t really mean not much.

To be specific, a BMI calculation takes the height and the weight of a person and uses that to determine if they weigh too much for their height. If you have a football player that is incredibly lean and muscular, their BMI will measure them as obese, when they are really not obese. So, **BMI is not an accurate measurement of fitness**. Body fat percentage, by contrast, is an accurate measurement of fitness. If you calculate your body fat as I have demonstrated, then you are left with your **lean body mass**, your LBM. Lean body mass is the actual goal of these measurements, and is necessary to calculate how much protein and fat you need in your diet. LBM is an essential factoid in determining your health, your lean body mass reflects your cellular health. Medical professionals consider cellular health to be your **vital capacity**, meaning how much oxygen you are moving through your cells and how much energy you are making.

> **[Graphic]** Slide "Your cellular energy production": glucose and oxygen go into the mitochondrion, which produces ATP (energy).

Observe the Cellular Energy Production image above. You may remember from high school Biology, the biological energy production of the cell. As a refresher, there are organelles, tiny organs in the cells, that actually create biological energy. These specific organelles are called mitochondria, the famed “Powerhouse” of the cell. In our image, the mitochondria are depicted as purple little sausage shaped organelles. The mitochondria require a steady supply of glucose, sugar, and oxygen in order to create ATP energy. ATP stands for **adenosine triphosphate**, and is all that the cell needs, with a few cofactors. Certain enzymes and vitamins are needed to help the mitochondria do its job.

The internal mitochondria is what produces the energy required for each cell, but there are multiple mitochondria per cell. Your muscles have the most mitochondria, while your nerves have many but less, and your heart has a lot of mitochondria being that it’s a muscle. As they are incredibly important they become damaged by toxins, as well as by viruses such as the cellular energy depleting Epstein-Barr virus. This process of cellular energy is essential both for your health and your fitness, and is influenced by your weight.

sections.text:
> **[Graphic]** Slide "Your hypothalamus controls your weight": silhouettes of people from very obese to lean, with a brain diagram pointing to the hypothalamus — the hypothalamus sets body weight.

You see, your hypothalamus controls your weight. It controls your weight by determining your **weight set point**. To illustrate this point, refer to this image of males, ranging from the morbidly obese to normal weight. The hypothalamus determines where on this scale you might find your body, by setting the weight set point according to your recent activity, not necessarily your ideal equilibrium. As an example, if you are trying to hibernate for the winter and you need to put on a lot more body fat to get your weight up in order to survive times of famine, then your hypothalamus will set your weight to be a little bit higher than your healthy norm to aid in this.

This will cause you to be heavier in your measurable weight, corresponding to an increase in body fat percentage. If this is necessary for survival, this increase is not a problem for your health. Your hypothalamus will stabilize on that weight set point, by lowering your energy expenditures, so that you do not waste any calories. Such a loss of calories could mean wintery death for our ancestors, whose biology we have inherited. If you **yo-yo diet,** meaning your weight raises and lowers erratically, then your hypothalamus will become confused. The hypothalamus will interpret this as you being in a time of stressful struggle and it will usually apply a higher weight set point in order to help you survive. This is why it is very difficult to lose weight if a person has been yo-yo dieting. They may experience a loss of 10 to 25 pounds and then gain this amount, often more, back again in short order. When in doubt, your hypothalamus is usually going to equalize your body at a slightly higher weight set point, in order to survive whatever is stressing you out and making your diet erratic. Your hypothalamus doesn't know you are dieting intentionally.

> **[Graphic]** Slide "Your hormones and your weight": a lean and a heavier woman back to back, surrounded by the glands that govern weight — hypothalamus and pituitary, adrenal glands, thyroid, ovary/testis, pancreas.

So, what does your hypothalamus do to control your weight? The Image to the left depicts the hypothalamus’ controls over your metabolism. The key to this complex system is the hypothalamic hormone **POMC.** POMC, also known as pro-opiomelanocortin, controls your pancreatic production of insulin, how much glucose your liver stores for later energy, and your thyroid’s production of hormones. POMC also controls your adrenal production of cortisol, the color of your skin and hair, as well as how sensitive your melanocytes are to day-night cycles. Whatever is left over from all of that hormone becomes beta-endorphins, or basically the happy neurotransmitters.

So, this single hypothalamic hormone controls your entire metabolic process through a cascade of other hormones. But, that is just one way the hypothalamus controls energy expenditure and the body’s weight. There are more methods that the hypothalamus controls your weight set point, via your hormones. How do your hormones control your weight? Well, your adrenal glands assist in surviving stressors, through the fight or flight mechanism. When a person is under an incredible amount of stress, they need to either get away or fight that stress and you produce cortisol in order to fuel this fight or flight choice. Cortisol’s role is to release the sugar stored in muscles and the liver, but not from the fat cells at this early fight or flight stage.

> **Are you taking notes? Let’s find out how accurate your notes and memory are:**
> - What does POMC stand for? Update your notes if you cannot find the answer there.
> - Name three hormones developed by your hypothalamus from POMC

So when do we use the sugar stored in fat cells? We use it when we need to respond to a stressor. But if we do not really need to fight or run away from danger, our bodies are going to release stored sugar that we do not otherwise need, and our bodies will then store it into our fat cells, usually right around the abdomen area. That is one way that our adrenal glands contribute to weight issues. Often times, during an acute stress you will lose weight first and then you will gain weight after the stressor is over.

The role of the pancreas is to produce insulin and glucagon. **Insulin** moves sugar into your cells, while **glucagon** removes the sugar from your cells. The Pancreas is always responsive to the blood sugar ratio in the system. Remember, that blood sugar (Glucose) is how cells produce energy. Our ovaries and testes need glucose, need that energy, and are responsive to how much stress you are under. The ovaries, as well, direct the body’s storage of fat, in order to produce enough estrogen to be fertile. Gonads do affects your weight, when necessary for reproduction.

Your Thyroid determines how quickly you burn energy, what is called the **basal metabolic rate,** through thyroid hormone production. The pituitary gland aids in this by producing **prolactin,** which helps to control your circadian rhythm. Your pituitary gland also produces growth hormone, which contributes to lean body mass. Remember that lean body mass, your muscles and your bones, is used to burn energy and is much more metabolically active than the energy stored in fat cells. On top of all of this is your hypothalamus, controlling all of these other glands.

sections.title: Genes
sections.text:
> **[Graphic]** Slide "Genes control your hunger and weight": the MC4R (written "MCR4") and FTO genes, with a brain image highlighting the hypothalamus and a DNA strand beside a figure made of molecules.

So, we all know, our genetic code controls our hunger and weight. While preparing the material for this document, I received an inquiry alleging the existence of “fatso genes”, which I found discouraging. The correspondent was referring to the FTO gene, “Fatso” being an inaccurate name, as these genes do not make a person fat or thin, but are around in your genetic code to help you survive. When we assign genes with these loaded nicknames, it implies the idea that our body is working “against us”. That is not true at all. Our genetic code is just trying to help us survive.

It is more helpful to think of the FTO gene as your “thrifty" gene. This is the gene that allows people to put on weight easily and survive those harsh winters. People who live in extreme Northern and Southern latitudes need this gene, as they face cold weather year round and may need to go without much vegetation for a long period of time. They better be able to put on body fat, or they will not survive. People who live near the equator tend to have a leaner body mass, because they do not really need to put on the body fat, their food supply is plentiful all year long. Of course, we are speaking in terms of generations and generations of adaptations to average conditions. As you can see, the FTO gene is really about survival.

The MC4R gene controls the melanocortin, the system that is sensitive to day and night cycles found within the hypothalamus. Those receptors are incredibly active in the hypothalamus, helping that organ determine if we are going into a period of winter or summer. Your melanocortin senses if you are getting enough sleep or if your body is actually under stress. From this sensory data, the hypothalamus constantly controls how much weight the body needs in order to survive. So, the MC4R and FTO genes can actually be controlled. I shall explain how, it is rather interesting.

It is essential to understand that the MC4R gene helps control your day-night cycles and your body mass index (skin color is governed by a related gene, MC1R). As previously explored, this index describes how much weight you hold relative to your height. If your energy levels are high, then you end up feeling like you are satiated: you are not hungry. This is because you are making energy and that energy will activate the MC4R gene. If your energy levels are low and you need to eat, then that also activates the MC4R gene, which dictates, “okay we need to eat.” Therefore, mutations in the MC4R gene can cause people to have a tendency to put on excess body fat.

Now the FTO gene controls the hunger hormone ghrelin. You experience the effects of Ghrelin when your tummy growls. Let us explore that growling tummy further. The FTO gene first increases the hunger hormone, **ghrelin**, while also suppressing the satiety hormone, **leptin**. Leptin is made in your body fat, suggesting a mechanism that allows your body to find equilibrium. People who carry two copies of the FTO risk variant tend to lose more weight through diet and lifestyle than those who carry only one copy. In other words, we can control our genes through our actions, by what we eat, and by how active we are. Our genes do not have control over us.

To illustrate this point, I want to reference a particular study performed in Spain. This study surveyed many hundreds of overweight people, measuring for FTO and MC4R mutations and those without. What the researchers found is that all of the overweight people had mutations in these genes, mutations that favored obesity. But those of this population who followed the traditional Mediterranean Food Pyramid and were **physically active** were still able to control their weight, despite the presence of the mutations. These subjects were able to lose weight. Now look at the above image of this traditionally-minded **Mediterranean Food Pyramid**. Notice that pasta is not in the bread portion, at the upper middle of the image. Pasta is actually found closer to the bottom, next to the veggie and fruit portion. The American perspective on Mediterranean Food is that bread include pasta. But that is not true, it’s not representative of the portions Mediterranean people eat pasta in.

Look again at the Mediterranean Food Pyramid, at the bottom you will see that the largest portion is the fruits and vegetables. Above that category you will find seeds, nuts, legumes, and olive oil. Above this you have fish and seafood, followed by the dairy portion. Then you have the starches, your breads, and your whole grain pasta. Then you have poultry and eggs, followed by the red meat. So, this is a very plant based diet and it actually favors staying thinner. The other big factor in the Mediterranean Food Pyramid found by these particular genetic studies is that the diet also includes red wine on a regular basis. From this it was determined that the combination of a plant-based diet with red wine, heavy in olive oil’s mono-unsaturated fats and low starches from breads and pasta, to be incredibly effective at turning off those thrifty genes, when combined with physical activity.

> **[Graphic]** Slide "What reverses the effect of fat genes": the Mediterranean food pyramid (a base of vegetables, fruits, olive oil, nuts and legumes; then fish; then dairy, grains and poultry; red meat at the small top) and physical activity of all kinds — boxing, yoga, cycling, tennis, walking the dog, stairs, running, dancing, mowing, sweeping, lifting, gardening.

> **Mediterranean Food Pyramid and YOU:**
> - Order your food groups into the portions you eat them in.
> - You may need to note down your regular diet for a week or two to have accurate notes
> - How does your pyramid compare to the MFP?

Physical activity is actually the key. If you are not physically active, then you are going to hold on to weight. In order to reverse the fat genes you need to combine the diet of the Mediterranean Food Pyramid combined with physical activity. The nutritional path to wellness is basically the Mediterranean Food Pyramid. The insulin resistance diet, is similar but removes the starches so that you can burn body fat while you are trying to jump start fat loss.

sections.title: The Hormones of Hunger
sections.text:
> **[Graphic]** Diagram "Leptin & ghrelin": before eating, ghrelin (made by the stomach/GI tract) is high and leptin (made by fat tissue) is low, tipping the balance toward hunger; after eating, leptin is high and ghrelin low, tipping it toward satiety (fullness).

Let us focus in on those hunger -causing hormones. Please refer to the image on the left. There are two such hormones, leptin and ghrelin. Leptin is produced in the fat, generally referred to as **adipose tissue.** As mentioned previously, Leptin is the hormone that triggers feelings of being satiated**.** By contrast, the hungry hormone, Ghrelin, is mainly produced in your stomach. Ghrelin controls the peristalsis, or the movement of food from your stomach into your small intestine and then on to the colon. This hormone specifically, is the trigger of hunger. Therefore, when you have more ghrelin in your system than you have leptin, you feel hungry. When the reverse is true, you feel satiated.

So, before you eat, your ghrelin is high and your leptin is low. After you eat, your ghrelin drops and your leptin rises. Remember that leptin is actually produced by your fat cells, and basically tells the hypothalamus that your body has enough fat storage. “We have already eaten.” it says, “You can stop feeding. You can stop eating.” That is a healthy message. But how does that explain people who just keep eating, even though they have eaten quite a bit of food. These people are over-eaters, also known as obsessive eaters, who tend to binge. What is going on in these people? In these people, there may be an imbalance between leptin and ghrelin or an insensitivity to leptin, they do not feel their leptin in their hypothalamus. They become desensitized to to this abundant hormone. Just as people become desensitized to insulin and become insulin resistant, as we have discussed.

Leptin affects your body broadly, including playing a role in how much thyroid hormone you produce, as well as in converting T4 into T3 which is the active form of thyroid hormone. So, your eating behavior is also affecting your thyroid. For instance, we know that anorexics who do not eat enough calories, their T3 levels are very very low. It is because their leptin has suppressed that conversion. Leptin tells your hypothalamus how much fat you are storing, and this influences fertility in women. So, leptin is going to help a woman’s body store a healthy amount of body fat for healthy pregnancies and if leptin sensitivity is off, her fertility will be affected. You need a certain amount of body fat in order to get pregnant, what is considered essential fat.

Now, leptin is trying to save your life. It is trying to keep you alive, helping you not to overeat and making sure you are eating enough. Ghrelin,which is also vital, induces high cortisol and high blood sugar. It induces the release of growth hormone. So, once you start to get hungry and you feel your tummy growl, that is ghrelin. The hunger hormone is in that moment trying to release sugar, to give the hypothalamus what it needs. Ghrelin is telling you that you need to eat to replace the sugar it just released. So, those hunger pangs are a part of your survival mechanism.

> **Hungry Hungry Hormones:**
> - Note down when you are hungry, when you eat for three days
> - Include generalized portions
> - Using this section, sketch what hunger hormones are peaking and diminishing throughout your day.

Neuropeptide Y is another hormone produced while your hungry. Neuropeptide Y actually controls hunger so drastically that it will actually lower your desire for sex. They have studied mice and found that if neuropeptide Y is stimulated enough the subject will choose to eat sugar over mating, a rare prioritization in the animal kingdom. We do know that neuropeptide Y actually controls both desires and this hormone is actually triggered when you restrict your calories. Therefore, when you go on a diet and you severely restrict your calories, you will crave sugar and your sex drive is going to drop. Neuropeptide Y does this through delaying your feeling of fullness, suppressing the effect of leptin. And so, your eating behavior is of primary concern when medically assisting in weight loss.

sections.text:
> **[Graphic]** Slide "What affects your hunger hormones": lack of sleep, stress, crash dieting.

I am going to touch on three things that affect your hunger hormones: Lack of sleep, stress, and crash dieting. Now you may notice that I did not introduce genetics as an equal factor in your hunger hormones, because these three factors allow you to influence that genetic factor. It helps a dieter to focus on what they can control, their sleep habits, how they handle stress, and whether what they put in their mouth is in their best interests.

So, the first hunger hormone trigger is the **lack of sleep**. Studies have found that people who actually sleep around seven to eight hours a day, they tend to have a healthy body mass index. What is more, they have normal leptin levels, normal hunger hormones, especially a normal level of ghrelin. However, the study found that those who sleep around five or less hours a night have a higher body mass index Again, this means those people are going to carry more weight for their relative height. They will also have less leptin, meaning less feelings of satiety, and so they cannot seem to tell their hypothalamus to stop eating. They also suffer an increase in ghrelin, the hunger hormone.

> **[Graphic]** Slide "#1 Hunger hormone trigger — lack of sleep": going from 8 to 5 hours of sleep is associated with BMI up 3.6%, leptin (fullness hormone) down 15.5% and ghrelin (hunger hormone) up 14.9%.

**Sleep** definitely affects how hungry you are. You may find if you have missed sleep that you tend to want to eat a little bit more sugar, you will want more starches. This reflects a biological attempt to stay awake during the day, through eating energetic foods. This biological process is due to the satiety hormone being suppressed and your hunger hormone being increased from low sleep, over time such a person will experience an increase in body fat.

Now, hunger hormone contributor number two? That would be **stress**. To understand the effects of stress on the body, keep in mind that stress is a perception of danger. For the hypothalamus stress indicates that the proverbial tiger is chasing you. A vast array of experiences can be perceived as stress. Whether it is that you are late for work, you have a deadline, you feel like your house is not clean enough, whatever is stressing you out, the hypothalamus responds the same way. “The tiger is chasing me.” the hypothalamus responds: “ I better get away.” And so immediately that organ triggers your adrenal glands to produce stress hormones. That immediately changes the effects of the hunger hormone ghrelin, how much insulin you produce and how much leptin you produce, which changes the expenditure of energy.

So, basically stress leads to the energy balance becoming off. When you need to get away from the danger, you are expending more energy than you are intaking. You do not have time to eat while you are running away from a tiger, so your body must use the stores of sugar in your muscles and in your liver toward that end. Too much stress over time will cause you to lose weight. But if that level of stress is not stable over time, the hypothalamus becomes desensitized to the stress. The hormone controlling organ will become resistant to the leptin and the body will start to expend less energy, holding on to more and more body fat. A stressful life, susceptible to as many stops as sudden starts. Sometimes, when the stressors are over, the person will start to gain some weight. So, the healthy response is to control our stress responses and that can be done through stress reduction techniques, which we will address in the Mindset section. Keep in mind that stress does affects the hunger hormones and resultant energy expenditure.

> **[Graphic]** Slide "#2 Hunger hormone trigger — stress": the brain balances energy expenditure against intake using signals from leptin (fat tissue), insulin (pancreas), ghrelin (stomach) and stress. (In the original graphic the leptin and insulin labels appear attached to the wrong organs.)

The third hunger hormone trigger is **crash dieting**. This is that vicious cycle, where a person fearing they are overweight begins dieting, which decreases your calories. This causes the **Famine Response**, which is to say that the body is losing weight not just from fat, but also losing weight from lean muscle tissue too. When this occurs, the metabolic rate starts to lower, because the system is intaking less calories from the diet, so the body counterproductively ends up storing more fat, as your hypothalamus thinks you must survive starvation.

A dieter seeing that they are not losing weight, often follows the Famine response with an increase of calories, as they slip back into their routine diet again. As far as the hypothalamus is concerned, now is the time for feasting. So, the reduced metabolic rate gained from dieting increases the muscle loss . Because the dieter lost muscle during their time of famine and they are not burning that energy, their body begins regaining weight from fat.

> **[Graphic]** Slide "#3 Hunger hormone trigger — crash dieting: the vicious diet cycle": diet (decrease in calories) → famine response (lose weight from lean muscle and fat, reduced metabolic rate, increased fat storage) → fall off (increase in calories) → feast response (reduced metabolic rate, loss of muscle, regain weight as fat) → overweight → repeat.

As an example, let us say that you had twenty pounds to lose, and you lost those twenty pounds over six months in a crash diet. Suppose you were eating 500 calories a day and you lost that twenty pounds really quickly. As soon as you start eating more than those 500 calories you are going to put on more body fat, because your hypothalamus believed you were starving, and the starvation is finally over.

Therefore, it is important not to yo-yo diet. And while I have outlined an insulin resistant diet as a basis to start the fat-loss process, I do not prefer to use the word diet. I find that “diet” carries too many connotations of the yo-yo cycle of dieting. “Diet” suggests that we are striving for lower weight, lower body fat, and so we are somehow sacrificing. For that sacrifice, dieters keep themselves from good foods. I would prefer to teach my patients and my students how to eat well. I prefer to identify nutritious foods and build them into a robust and long term eating habit. So, there is no reason to “diet”, instead we focus on taking in less calories, specifically those found in starches. If you start following a healthy nutritional plan at all times, not intermittently, you can stop the yo-yo cycle. Use the insulin resistance diet to pull off a little fat, then graduate on to the Mediterranean Food Pyramid to keep your calorie intake healthy, only adding those starches a little bit at a time.

#### Controlling the Hunger Hormones
> **[Graphic]** Slide "How to control your hunger hormones": a glass of water (hydrate), "Stop yo-yo dieting," a small pile of dark round fruits, and "Eat your fiber" (vegetables, fruits, legumes and whole grains).

How do we control our hunger hormones? Well, of course the first step is to stop the yo-yo dieting! We have all been in that situation when we have tried over and over again to try to lose weight, and when that invariably does not work we just try a new diet. That is the vicious cycle of dieting at large. We may try a Keto diet, then an Atkins diet, then we try a Zone Based diet, or we try the South Beach diet; we tried it all. This comes from the false impression that we must learn how to eat from another person, instead of **listening to our bodies**, which are trying to save us.

So dear reader, the next thing I want you to do in this moment is to tell your body “I surrender to you, body, I know you know what is best in terms of keeping me alive. Please, show me what you need me to eat!” I find with my patients who are taking Genesis Gold that your body is going to start talking to you.

We just have to get over our bad habits, that are feeding the fat cells and not feeding our lean body mass. It is essential to eat what are known as **Core Foods**. Studies conducted on the standard American diet, also known as SAD, found that the Standard American Diet tends to deregulate our hunger hormones and upregulates your fat genes. A historian will note the size of our plates have increased over time. Have you ever been to an antique store and noticed how tiny the dinner plates are, they are the size of our lunch plates now. And how long ago was that? Antiques are defined by being at least fifty years old. Therefore, it was not even a century ago that we started increasing the size of our portions. Everything is about “supersizing” and now more and more food that we expect to eat in our stomachs just accept all that.

I call this state of affairs the SAL (Standard American Lifestyle), in addition to the SAD. We not only eat SAD, a diet high in trans fats and starches yet low in plant based foods, but we also sit around and are not very physically active. These two factors together are made worse by not getting the sleep we desperately need because we are on our devices too late, watching television, and not getting enough sleep in total darkness. Also, we are constantly feeling stressed, we do not relax, nor do we know how to relax. When we put all that together with a Standard American Lifestyle then you have triggered the hunger hormones to create a constant feeding behavior. And so, changing our lifestyle is really critical to changing our Body Mass Index.

One of the biggest changes we can affect is to begin eating more fiber, conjoined with a plant based diet of course. In a plant based diet, eaters derive their fiber from whole grains, nuts, seeds, and legumes. Plants in their original and whole form will provide these fibers, both vegetables and fruit. As an advisory, you are not going to get these fibers from drinking the juices of those plants, unless you are juicing with a machine that preserves the whole fiber . Even then, nutritionally speaking, drinking the juice will never give the full benefit of eating the plant it is made from. After all, juices are only the sugars and vitamins of the plant.

Now what else could one do to ease down their BMI? One of the tricks to controlling ghrelin, the growling hunger hormone, is as simple as drinking a big glass of water before you eat. Ghrelin not only controls your hunger, it also controls your thirst mechanism. If you think back and apply this principle, you may recall some times when you have been really thirsty and not hungry, where satiating the thirst calmed your hunger. It is an old diet trick but it works due to the effect on ghrelin. You can usually satiate that hunger hormone if you drink a big glass of water, a healthy 8 ounces, before you eat. We can lower the ghrelin's effects. Drink enough water, and you will feel like the smaller portion of food satiates you as larger portions used to.

> **Recipe: Deborah's Cocoa Energy Balls**
>
> *Created for Phase I of the Insulin Resistant Diet.*
>
> **Mix:**
> - 1½ cups raw organic cocoa (raw, cold-processed)
> - 2 cups organic nut butter — depending on how oily the nut butter is, you may need to add 1–4 tbsp coconut oil
> - 1 cup coconut and hemp hearts, to bind the dough
> - About 4 tbsp raw honey — taste the dough and sweeten to taste
>
> **Make:** Roll into balls about the size of a golf ball. Makes approximately 3 dozen. Store in a covered container, separating layers with wax paper. Refrigerate and enjoy.
>
> **About 120 calories per ball.**
>
> **Why these ingredients:** The raw cocoa helps increase serotonin, which suppresses sugar cravings. The small amount of raw, locally grown honey helps your immune system adapt to your environment. The coconut is rich in MCT, a type of fat that helps reverse insulin resistance. The nut butters provide a balance of protein and fat to prevent hyperglycemia (a high blood sugar surge after eating).

Another trick are what I call “**cocoa energy balls**”. If you have recently eaten and know you ate enough, yet you still feel hungry, this is because your body has yet to release the stored sugar in your liver, which signals your hypothalamus that you have just eaten. This trick is to eat a little bit of sugar right after your meal, just as most cultures have dessert after they eat when it’s available. Sugar stops the feeding behavior in its tracks.

Therefore, for my patients who are trying to lose weight, I have designed these “cocoa energy balls”. My recipe uses the effect of cocoa to raise serotonin levels, giving you a good mood, with the effects of honey to give the hypothalamus that sugar signal. I bake both into the fiber of the coconut and nut butter, so the package of sugar is wrapped around protein and fat. This allows the sugar to ride on the fiber a little bit longer, to come to effect over a longer period of digestion.

This recipe really works, especially if you are hungry right after lunch. If you are still looking for carbohydrates to munch on, yet you are on that insulin resistant diet, having a “cocoa energy ball” right after lunch can satisfy that feeling. If you tend to want sweets right after dinner; perhaps your sleep habits rely on sweets, having a cocoa energy ball after dinner will raise serotonin levels which will convert over to melatonin and help you sleep better. This trick is born of experience. Sugar, especially in the form of chocolate, makes a big difference to a patient’s appetite. Dark chocolate especially so, which is why we use rock cocoa in the “cocoa energy balls”.

> **[Graphic]** Slide "Your gut flora influences your mood": the intestines and the brain connected by bands of light — the gut–brain connection.

So, what about your gut flora, does our gut bacteria affect our body fat? Of course! You see, the microbes you have inside your gastrointestinal tract, they strive to survive. If these bacterium are beneficial to you, then they are perfect for what you are eating. But if you have pathogens or bacteria that do not really belong inside you and are not beneficial to your healthy functions, they will attempt to turn their environment to their favor, and trigger your desire for the foods that favor them.

These organisms do in fact cause a hunger for foods that help them survive, and even thrive. I find a great deal of food cravings are not native to the patient, in this way. These hankerings for junk food can be bacteria in your gut asking for sugar, for fats, for salts, for starches, and (usually) carbs. There was an interesting study performed on mice where the fecal matter, containing the gut bacteria, from one mouse was implanted in the digestive tract of another mouse. The findings showed that giving the gut bacteria from an obese mouse to a thin mouse causes the thin mouse to become obese. The bacteria from the obese mouse will cause the thin mouse to start eating unhealthy nutrients to feed this foreign culture. These effects have been observed in humans as well.

So, part of healing your issues of losing body fat is healing your gastrointestinal tract and improving your gut flora. One method is to implant the gut flora that are actually beneficial to the patient instead of trying to get their host to feed themselves junk which guides the patient to gorge. Controlling a patient's gut flora is a critical step. Research shows that our gut flora affects our moods. If you do not eat as your internal ecology asks several things may happen. You will become moody, you may get sad, you will get emotional, you may even get angry and rageful. Unfortunately, the only method to suppress this effect is to eat what your microbial stowaways want you to eat.

My patients that cannot stop themselves from eating starches invariably have an issue with their gut flora. So, please keep this factor in mind when getting help to control your weight and ask to investigate how healthy your onboard bacterium is. Are these stowaways working for you, or against you? The microbes in our illustrated image to the left are asking for the Standard American Diet, rather than the healthier Mediterranean Food Pyramid. The SAL is another factor that affects your internal culture’s effect on your weight, such as American overreliance on antibiotics, coupled with a lack of fermented foods in our diet that are needed to-replenish our beneficial gut flora after antibiotic use. Correcting your gut flora imbalances could go a long way toward helping a dieter to get their weight under control, their body fat down, and increasing their lean body fat mass.

> **[Graphic]** Slide "Gut flora controls your food intake": cartoon gut microbes with speech bubbles craving pizza, a burger and a cookie — gut bacteria drive cravings.

sections.text:
Everyone wants to know the healthiest diet, but I have already shown it to you; The Mediterranean Food Pyramid. In the image of this pyramid to the left, I have added the previously mentioned glass of wine. Studies have shown that the **red wine** combined with the Mediterranean Food Pyramid actually does make a difference to lowering Body Mass Index. If you have been fortunate enough to visit a Mediterranean country, you may notice that the people do not struggle with obesity in the numbers we do in America. Mediterraneans really are thinner possibly because they tend to be more active, but absolutely because of their diet.

> **[Graphic]** Slide "2) Best diet for healthy weight": the Mediterranean food pyramid and a glass of red wine — plant-based; healthy fats about 30–40% (monounsaturated olive oil); adequate protein; anti-inflammatory red wine; few processed foods.

You may also have noticed the many vegetables that are served in Mediterranean food. Fruits, vegetables, nuts, seeds and legumes, all are abundant in the Mediterranean diet, while red meat is served in tiny portions. Even the famous pasta of the Mediterranean diet is served in similarly tiny proportions, compared to what we serve. Neither the pasta nor starch is the base of this diet. How does that translate to your own meals?

When looking at your dinner plate, the goal is to have vegetables and whole plants covering at least half of your plate. The next smallest portion should be the legumes, followed by nuts, seeds and olive oil. fish and dairy are the next smallest share, even less non vegetable starch. The two smallest additions would be a little bit of poultry, ending with a tiny bit of red meat. You can add only a glass of wine a night, for health. Wine has been shown to help with those fat genes, particularly red wine. So, the Mediterranean Food Pyramid is full of healthy fats and, of course, this breakdown should not describe every meal.

So, this is the diet I have chosen in my life, and I came upon this diet in my own Mediterranean heritage. I am married to a Greek man, hence my last name Maragopoulos, though my heritage is Italian. Working with my own diet, and using the Mediterranean Food Pyramid, I basically came up with **DMAR Nutritional Path to Wellness**. The essentials are to eat enough protein and fat for your lean body mass while eating a variety of colorful and locally organic grown fresh foods and vegetables. The Nutritional path includes limiting your grains and starches to meet your activity level and avoiding man-made carbohydrates, artificial sweeteners, processed foods and trans fats.

So, if you have previously calculated your body fat, you can use the chart on the right to calculate the carbs needed by your lean body mass. Simply, weight times whatever your body fat is equals your pounds of body fat. Your weight minus your pounds of body fat is your lean body mass. That number is how many pounds of lean body mass you have. If you had 100 pounds of lean body mass, you would then need 0.5 to 1 gram (per pound of lean body mass) of protein and a half gram per pound of lean body mass of fat, in order to maintain that body mass.

My patients are always asking me “how many carbs should I have for the day? How much should I basically be eating in terms of carbohydrates”? To answer this for you, remember that carbohydrates come from plants, from starches, and essentially from sugars. Now, your whole plants do not count towards any carbohydrate total. I am only talking about carbohydrates that come from starches such as your grains, pastas, rices, breads, and legumes (which are starches and sugars). I do not care about the fiber, either. I am only looking at total carbohydrates minus fiber, that is your net carbs total for the day.

> **[Graphic]** Slide "DMAR Nutritional Path to Wellness — your activity level determines how many carbs you eat": overweight/sedentary 45 g/day; overweight/active 45–90 g/day; sedentary 45–90 g/day; ideal weight but with an "insulin meter" of belly fat 45–90 g/day; ideal weight/inactive 90–135 g/day; ideal weight/athletic 105–290 g/day.

> **[Graphic]** Slide "DMAR Nutritional Path to Wellness — lean body mass (LBM) determines protein and fat": protein 0.5–1 g per lb of LBM; fat 0.5 g per lb of LBM. Eat a variety of colorful, locally grown, organic fresh fruits and vegetables; limit grains and starchy vegetables to your activity-based carb needs; avoid manmade carbs, artificial sweeteners, processed foods and trans fats.

Let us look at quinoa, as an example, only half a cup of quinoa. Quinoa has about twenty-one grams of carbohydrates per half cup, but four of those grams are fiber. So, the net carbohydrates for half a cup of quinoa is 17 grams. If you are looking for net carbohydrates, that is what you are trying to pay attention to. If you are overweight and/or sedentary, as you may be if you sought out this document, you are allocated 45 grams of carbohydrates per day. This is important, because you must lower your carbohydrates to get fat cells to lose their long held cargo.. Sitting on your rear end and not moving burns hardly any energy. You need those 45 grams just to stay alive, any more becomes excess. If you’re eating more than that you’re going to gain body fat. If you are overweight while active and you need more grams of carbohydrates, anywhere between 45 and 90 grams of net Carbohydrates. Your activity throughout the day will determine where your energy needs are in that range. That net total is per day, not per meal.

> **Math this!**
> - Calculate your BMI
> - Calculate your Lean Body Mass
> - Use these numbers to drive your daily allotment of carbohydrates
> - Note any changes you need to make in your diet.

I will give you another example. If you eat sweetened yogurt, you might think that yogurt is normally healthy, right? But yogurt that has been sweetened will have carbs in it, usually a cup of yogurt has about 40 to 45 grams of carbohydrates per cup, from sugar alone. You want to stay away from those added sugars, because every bit of carbs counts. If you are sedentary, then 45 to 90 grams of carbohydrates is the max that you can healthily eat.

Let’s say you are at an ideal weight, but you have that insulin meter fat, that is to say you have got the belly roll, also known as the muffin top. The only solution to losing this is to limit your carbohydrates to between 45 to 90 grams , in order to burn that insulin meter down per day. If you are at an ideal weight, but you are inactive/ sedentary, then you are going to want 90 to about 135 grams per day in order to maintain your lean body mass and feed your activity level. If you are at an ideal weight and you are athletic, the chart above shows how much more carbohydrates your metabolism can handle: a hearty 105 to 290 grams per day.

I know this from my experience as a triathlete because of the negative hormone effects related to my unhealthily low 12% body fat. I did not have periods at all, due to that low body fat. I had to eat quite a bit of carbohydrates just to keep my energy levels up since I was constantly training for a triathlon. Younger me was running 20 miles at a time, or bicycling 75 miles at a time, or swimming two miles at a time, each of which required a massive expenditure of carbohydrates. Had I been unable to keep up, I would have begun to burn into my body fat, and I needed that body fat to survive. So, these are the circumstances in which you can take in extra carbohydrates, which medical professionals recommend for long distance athletics. The majority of Americans are carb loading with all the bread, pasta, and rice that they are eating, with no activity outlet. These people are getting way too many carbohydrates and if they are not exercising then they are not burning it off. The body must be storing it.

sections.text:
> **[Graphic]** Slide "3) Physical activity": aerobics 3 times a week (HIIT is perfect); one "LSD" per week — long slow distance in nature; get up every hour for 5 minutes to walk, stretch, move; three 10-minute walks a day are as effective as 30 minutes of exercise for sustained weight loss.

Speaking of triathlons and burning carbohydrates: **Physical activity**, it makes you more metabolically active, which means that you can eat more calories. This activity is key and goes hand in hand with your diet. Here is what I recommend: Aerobics three times a week, is one option. HIIT movements are perfect for burning body fat and increasing lean body mass. Next, One LSD per week -not the drug, of course – that’s one Long Slow Distance walk per week. What Ienjoy is using such activity to go into nature, take a walk in a park, take a hike on reserved land, or a long slow bicycle ride on the streets of your hometown.

What a long slow distance activity without the high aerobics, like a leisurely hike, does is induce your fat stores to burn energy. If you engage your body in this way once a week, then you are training your body to go into your fat stores to burn energy. As you pass 30 minutes of continuous movement, muscle glycogen levels gradually dip, and the relative proportion of energy derived from fat oxidation increases. Low-intensity aerobic exercise uses a higher percentage of fat as fuel, while higher-intensity exercise (like HIIT or running) burns more total calories and total fat overall, plus triggers the afterburn effect.

One thing that medical professionals have noticed in obesity and fitness studies is that if a person is sitting around all day long they will invariably gain fat over time. If they get up every hour and move around for about five minutes by stretching or walking they break that steady gain of fat and become more metabolically active. We also know that, in the case of people who do exercise thirty minutes a day -five days per week - if they break that thirty minutes into three ten minute cycles per day, the activity is just as effective at weight loss as an LSD activity a week. They may not lose weight as quickly as those with dedicated long distance activity , but they will still sustain weight loss in their stored fat.

People who are overweight that have gone through such studies where half of the group was given thirty minutes of exercise to perform five days a week while the other half of the group had to break it up and do three 10 minute walks, five days a week, saw interesting results. After six months, the subjects who exercised thirty minutes of time had lost more body fat and a little more weight than those who broke up their exercise into five chunks a week. But, after a year, the ten minute at three times a day walkers had continued to sustain that weight loss, while the thirty minute a day exercisers saw a drop off in lost weight. They just were not losing weight at the same rate anymore. Therefore; just taking walks once a morning, then at lunch, and again maybe after dinner is very healthy. These recall the constitutional walks that past generations took part in after meals, supposedly to “keep the meals moving”. The exercise does indeed help the digestion, on a metabolic level.

> **Calculate yourself:**
> - Use a pedometer or fitness tracker to note your exercise periods throughout the week
> - Note which pattern of exercise discussed in this section matches yours most closely
> - What changes do you need to make

We know that you will become obese if you decrease your energy expenditure if you are eating more calories than you use up, even if only by 50 to 150 extra calories a day. This is only five percent of most people’s daily caloric intake. That tiny extra is all it takes to move toward obesity. But, similarly, all you need to do to counteract this effect is get up and walk a little bit, fifteen short walks a week makes a huge difference. You might even consider using a fitness worn monitor to inform you of how many steps you take.

Let me tell you a story about my experience with handheld pedometers. My father had procured a couple of cheap pedometers at a dollar store and gave one to me. He spent the next weekend doing some handyman tasks for me while my husband was away on a trip. We were both were wearing our little pedometers that weekend and decided to take a walk to compare how many steps we took. Since we decided to take our dogs with us it became a few miles walk. When we returned home, we found that my total came a little short to my dad’s, though I had taken more steps than him. His handyman tasks made us mostly equivalent, at approximately 3,000 steps. After this, dad sat down at my computer and checked his email while I was busy with a load of laundry to wash and fold then feed the horses and pets. Keep in mind that I do not have a big piece of property, maybe an acre to walk there and back. Finally, I went out to the garden to pick some vegetables for dinner and then started making that dinner. We compared our pedometers at the end of the night, my dad had increased his steps by just a couple hundred of steps. He had not really moved very much from the computer to the dinner, from the table to the bathroom, or to the bed. I, on the other hand, had doubled my steps due to my level of energy while taking care of these chores. My father jokingly asked if I had gone for another walk without him, but the truth was that I had been running around doing all the chores and getting things ready for dinner and feeding animals. It all adds up. Just being active makes a huge difference. So, just start moving. That will burn the calories, burn the fat, and will increase your basal metabolic rate and help you to increase your lean body mass and lower your body fat.

#### Restorative Sleep
> **[Graphic]** Slide "4) Get enough sleep": sleep at least 7.5 hours every night, in the dark, to increase melatonin and decrease insulin resistance; good sleep lowers hunger hormones.

Then we have the all important factor of **sleep**. We know you need at least seven and a half hours of sleep every night in the dark in order to maintain a healthy body fat to lean body mass ratio. If you do not get enough sleep, you will eventually gain weight. We know this because people who work night shifts such as nurses, police officers, firemen, and those who have to stay up for long periods of time (then miss sleep during the day) are more likely to develop insulin resistance, increased body fat, and have trouble losing weight.

If you are sleeping in the dark you are making more melatonin. When you make more melatonin, you decrease your insulin resistance and start burning your body fat. We know that, if you get enough sleep it lowers your hunger hormones, and so you will not be as hungry. So, rather than eating more, sleep more – it makes a big difference in how much energy you are going to burn and how much body fat you are going to carry.

sections.text:
Finally, **mindset** is our last pillar. This is the other piece of the Mediterranean lifestyle, compared to the standard American lifestyle. Mediterranean people eat together by sitting down and taking time to eat their meals, rather than eating in front of a television or the computer. Fast Food is antithetical to the Mediterranean lifestyle so there is much less eating fast food compared to America. I remember the very first time my husband and I went to Greece and Italy in 2001. It was right after the tragic events of September 11th, though we travelled anyhow because it was a trip that we had planned for a long time.

> **Exercise your mind-set!**
> - List three beliefs you have about food that are not easily scientifically substantiated
> - List three more beliefs on how you eat
> - List three people you would like to eat with more regularly

As Americans, we were really shocked that we were not able to get to-go cups in Italy. If you were going to get coffee there, you had to sit down in the coffee shop or the little café and drink the coffee in that moment. There was no to-go coffee. Certainly these countries have that now, but at the time it was a foreign the concept is to them. I was really impressed with that because I realized that is part of our societal health issues.

We Americans are actually consuming calories as we are running around. Our body is never settling down to perceive a differentiation between our activity and our eating behavior. So, eating in social group together, with gratitude, really makes a difference. You are blessing your food with this mindset, you are passing that benefit to your body, it pays attention to what you believe and what you think.

> **[Graphic]** Slide "5) Healing mindset for healthy metabolism" (photo of a large family meal outdoors): you are what you eat and what you think; eat together with gratitude; visualize a healthy, fit you; be grateful to your body fat for saving you, and then let it go.

As true as it is that you are what you eat, is that you are what you think. Visualize a healthy fit you and be grateful to the body fat that you have now, because it has kept you safe, and it is time to let it go. Like a boat or a buoy, your fat helping you float around the river of consciousness, through life. Your fat got you through your stressors. The people who cannot hold on to that healthy weight are probably going to die. The people who can maintain a healthy weight are going to be the survivors. So let it go. Thank your fat and let it go. Use the Five Pillars of Hormonal Healing to lose your excess body fat. You can keep your metabolism healthy with [Genesis Gold](https://genesisgold.com/genesisgold/).
