When medical professionals test for thyroid dysfunction we measure TSH, free T4, and free T3, but not the totals. The reason the totals are not used is because free T4 and T3 are the active hormones, while totals would include reverse T3. Reverse T3 tests make sure that you are not producing too much reverse T3, in proportion to your free T3 levels. If we suspect the patient to have autoimmunity then we will check **thyroid peroxidase antibodies**, **thyroglobulin**, and **thyroglobulin antibodies (**aka TGB in the image above). It can be helpful to think about the thyroid as a seesaw, a negative feedback system, to better understand the reasoning. If the TSH is elevated than the T4 and T3 is too low for a healthy body. An elevated TSH indicates that your pituitary gland is not getting enough T4 and T3.

If both the TSH is low and the T4 and T3 are low then the body is suffering miscommunication of the hypothalamic-pituitary interaction. I find this to be common among my incoming patients. Therefore, I do not recommend only checking TSH. I check TSH, free T4, and free T3 in all of my patients to form a baseline. I will add the rest of these factors to the test, such as the reverse T3 and antibodies if I suspect a patient has thyroid disorder or autoimmunity.

sections.text:

A moving thyroid is like a butterfly lying upon the trachea. Thyroid imaging is called for when the medical professional feels a mass on the thyroid. This imaging study uses an **ultrasound** to take a picture of the thyroid to visually confirm a cyst or enlargement in the thyroid. sections.text:
> **[Graphic]** Slide "What's a goiter?": illustration of a woman with a swollen neck, comparing a normal thyroid with an enlarged thyroid (goiter).

What is a goiter? Notice in the picture to the left that this woman’s neck is notably swollen. Goiters often look this large, or larger. Of course not everyone with a chubby neck has a goiter. Goiters cause a swelling in the lower part of the neck. Normally, your thyroid is right above your collar bones and it is right underneath what would be the Adam’s apple in the male. The thyroid can be felt as a thick extension of the Adam’s apple directly underneath that structure. If masculine readers followed the exercise to feel your thyroid, as above, when they put their hands on their throat they probably felt the thyroid as an enlargement. Not only does your practitioner feel that, but some goiters can be seen if they have become grossly enlarged.

Goiters are usually associated with a **low iodine diet** because the thyroid is growing in search of the iodine it needs. If the levels of TSH are higher than normal, then this is stimulating the thyroid to make more T4. Without the iodine resources it needs to meet these requests, the thyroid grows. However, the same thing will happen in cases of hyperthyroidism. Goiters are one of those health issues we need to pay attention to: a goiter from iodine deficiency can be easily treated with iodine, but extra iodine can worsen Hashimoto’s or Graves’.

sections.title: Autoimmune Thyroiditis
sections.text:
> **[Graphic]** Slide "Autoimmune thyroiditis." Hashimoto's disease: an enlarged, inflamed, underactive thyroid (goiter) — TSH and TPO antibodies go up, T4 and T3 go down. Graves' disease: an enlarged, inflamed, overactive thyroid (goiter) with bulging eyes — TSH goes down, while TSI (thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulin), T4 and T3 go up.

The image to the right depicts what two types of autoimmune thyroiditis look like when manifested in the body. Both **Hashimoto’s Disease** (an autoimmune cause of low thyroid production) and Graves disease have a tendency to develop goiters in enlarged thyroid. In the image we see normal size thyroid transposed over enlarged thyroids. We also see photographs of their presentation under the skin. Both Hashimoto’s & Graves disease can be cystic and lumpy. In the Grave’s disease image we can see the person affected has notable white around her eyes due to bulging. In **Graves’ disease** (high thyroid productions) the TSH will always be suppressed while T4, T3 and TSI will be drastically elevated. **TSI** is an antibody produced in Graves’ disease that stimulates the TSH receptor, mimicking TSH.

Both of these diseases were named after the doctors who discovered them; they are autoimmune causes of hyperthyroidism (Graves’) and hypothyroidism (Hashimoto’s). In cases of hypothyroidism the body’s TSH is elevated, as elevated TPO antibodies are normal, the T4 and T3 amounts are going to be low. Although these symptoms may not show as notably low, I have seen patients with early Hashimoto’s disease that I suspect to also have hypothyroidism. Their blood levels are fine, their individual T4, T3, or TSH may show as fine, but their TPO antibodies are elevated.

If a patient’s thyroid feels a little inflamed to my examination, they complain that swallowing feels like they must swallow “over something”, they feel like they are almost choking on something, or they notice their thyroid more when self examining the neck, I suspect hypothyroidism and know what to do. I check those **antibodies**, which are usually slightly elevated in these cases. These patients are heading towards autoimmunity.

Any more than 15 g of soy protein in a person suffering from any of the above will interfere with T3 activity.

In order to have healthy hormones and healthy thyroid production we need to balance our hypothalamus. The main transitions we go through in the course of our lives that shift us biochemically, emotionally and spiritually can be seen above. In this document we will focus on three aspects in each transition. These transitions are **puberty**, period, pregnancy, pause, and the poof. sections.title: Hormones and Immunity
related_qa: MOOD-01 to MOOD-04, STR-01 to STR-07
sections.text:
> **[Graphic]** Slide "Hormones affect your immunity": optimal immunity sits in the middle (with a jar of Genesis Gold). Over-reaction to an internal threat = autoimmunity; over-reaction to an external threat = allergies; under-reaction to an internal threat = cancer; under-reaction to an external threat = infection.

As your hormones shift through your life, they shape your body in interesting ways. Primarily, hormones affect your immunity. Patients and students going through these changes will ask me, “What is happening to me when I am going through a hormonal change like perimenopause? What will occur with my immunity?” Understand that hormones affect your immunity, causing the immune system to underact and to overact. observe the graphic above to the right, where you can see optimal immunity in the middle. If the body is **underreacting** to something inside your body this can potentially develop into a cancer. If the immune cells are not cleaning house as they should, the system may develop a few cells that could be cancerous. This occurs on a nearly daily basis that a healthy immune system gets rid of these cancerous cells; if it does not, cancer could develop.

If the immune system is underreacting to an external threat from outside of the body, that can result in an infection. What if the immune system is overreacting? Well, overreaction to external threat, like pollens or foods, manifests as an allergy or a hypersensitivity. Overreacting to an internal threat, such as attacking the thyroid or the joints like rheumatoid arthritis, that is an autoimmunity. Optimally, **the immune system requires balance**, not overreacting or underreacting, which requires your hormones to be balanced.

> **[Graphic]** Slide "Hormones affect your brain": hormones (testosterone, estrogen, progesterone, prolactin/melatonin, DHEA/cortisol, HGH, T4/T3) influence brain neurotransmitters (norepinephrine, dopamine, serotonin, acetylcholine, GABA, oxytocin). Images of a male and a female brain.

The hormones also affect the brain. The hormones listed on the right in the image below correspond to the neurotransmitters on the right hand side. We know that the following hormones affect the brain’s chemistry:

- The gonadal hormones testosterone, estrogen and progesterone

- The pituitary and pineal hormones prolactin and melatonin

- The adrenal hormones DHEA and cortisol

- Human growth hormone, which is a pituitary hormone

- Thyroid hormones T4 and T3.

These hormones literally activate and deactivate these brain chemicals. **Norepinephrine** is the brain’s adrenaline, dopamine for learning, as well as the memory hormone produced mainly during the daytime. **Serotonin** is not only the “happy” hormone, but the focus hormone, giving our brains the ability to focus and concentrate. **Acetylcholine** supports memory, including subconscious memory, and I believe it plays a role in the “divine experience.” **GABA** is what de-intensifies the brain’s chemistry and calms our brain. Drugs like Xanax and Valium work by stimulating the GABA receptor, which may increase dependency on the drugs. Note that progesterone activates GABA. Oxytocin rises when a woman is breastfeeding, creating the feeling of bonding they experience, but it also rises after sexual intercourse or orgasm when we feel bonded to our partners. It also rises when we get hugs. These neurochemicals have hormonal triggers.

sections.title: Transitions and Symbolism
sections.text:
> **[Graphic]** Artwork of the triple goddess — Maiden (young woman in white with flowers), Mother (pregnant woman in red) and Crone (older woman in black with a cauldron) — under waxing, full and waning moons: symbols of a woman's life stages.

To begin, I would like you to turn your attention to the graphics showing two gendered trios. We see the maiden, mother, crone, but how are these mythic figures relevant? They demonstrate the three main transitions in a woman’s life: developing as a child in to a maiden, meaning going through puberty, producing a young woman. Women become a mother in their reproductive years, and the crone, or as we would more politely call her, an old lady. **The crone is an important figure in many cultures**, modeling aging gracefully instead of what some currently see as insulting. Older cultures might say, when we are done bleeding out our wisdom every month, we are crowned in wisdom. A croning ceremony was a crowning ceremony, welcoming the figure as a wise woman in the Council of local elders.

For men, European culture offers this medieval symbolic model. I Found this model in a book that helped me to understand male psychology a little bit better. It was written by a female psychologist who wrote it in novel form, describing the transition of men through this medieval model. The boy is a page, going through puberty. Next the boy becomes the knight, trying to conquer everything. Then the knight becomes a prince, trying to build his kingdom, career, and/or family. Then the father passes and the prince becomes the king later in life. **These three masculine steps that are congruent with the female steps.** Next, we will discuss each of these, as well as their spiritual aspects.

> **[Graphic]** Historical illustration of three medieval men — a knight in armor with a shield, a crowned king with a sword, and a robed elder — representing the masculine life stages (page → knight → prince → king).

sections.title: Puberty
sections.text:
> **[Graphic]** Slide "Puberty — the beginning." Girls: body odor, pubic hair, breast buds, body fat, menses (ages 9–16, average 12), growth spurt within 2 years. Boys: body odor, pubic hair, scrotum changes, nocturnal emissions (ages 10–14, average 12), growth spurt within 4–6 years.

Puberty, of course, comes first. A**ll people develop body odor and pubic hairs develop**. In girls, breast buds are developing, just as scrotum structure changes in boys. Young girls and boys will experience a shift in their body fat; but for young girls, this fat growing on their hips and their thighs is essential for storage of the estrogen needed for the menstrual period. The menstrual period usually begin anywhere from nine to sixteen years of age. The average age for entering puberty is about 12 for girls and boys. Though boys may not have any blood to show for it, most will instead experience nocturnal emissions, also known as wet dreams as this time. Wet dreams indicate that testosterone levels are rising toward adult levels. A young girl’s growth spurt will happen within two years after she starts her menstrual cycle, and for a young boy growth takes four or six years. This is why smaller boys can graduate from high school, but return for a reunion having grown quite a bit, because he reached his growth spurt later.

Looking further into puberty, we need to understand what is happening in the adolescent body, mind, and soul. The adolescent body desperately requires adequate nutrition. A Mediterranean diet is one of the best diets for young people as it provides a variety of nutrients. These come from a wide variety of fruits and vegetables, but adolescents also need adequate fat and adequate protein. Young girls will crave carbohydrates to make more estrogen, while young boys will crave protein so they make more testosterone. Of course, **these kids need a lot of sleep**. They need way more sleep than adults do and; unfortunately, it is hard for them to get that when we send them to school much too early. Adolescents’ melatonin levels will not drop off at 7 or 8 o’clock in the morning, but more like 9 o’clock, making early rising very difficult.

> **[Graphic]** Slide "Thriving puberty." Adolescent body: adequate nutrition, enough sleep, enough activity, a nontoxic environment. Adolescent mind: "What's happening to me?" — the adolescent brain needs sleep and good fat. Adolescent soul: separation from parents, establishing identity — the girl's child becomes the Maiden; the boy's page becomes the Knight. Banner: Deborah teaches that Genesis Gold helps the pubescent body and brain through the hormonal roller coaster.

Adolescents need to get activity into their bodies regularly, and if they become stagnant at this point in their life they are going to have more problems with their hormones. **This comes with weight issues later on in life**. So encouraging them to be physically active can be very supportive. They do not necessarily have to be an athlete, but they must move those young growing bodies in order to have healthy bodies later in life.

It is important that young people are not exposed to excess toxins because those toxins can act as **endocrine disruptors**, meaning that the toxins interfere with their hormones and the youths will develop hormonal issues. Endocrine disruptors from plastics, pesticides and hormones in animal products are linked to earlier puberty in girls, which may raise breast cancer risk later in life.

> **Puber-me?:**
> - Make a list of Puberty changes you endured as a teenager
> - Mark each one that felt insurmountable at the time
> - Now X each one that eventually passed. Compare with your marks.

So what is happening to the adolescent mind? They are fixated and overwhelmed by the transition they are going through, and having no prior experience to relate it to. Puberty creates an internal emotional and psychological roller-coaster. **The adolescent brain needs sleep and good fat in order for it to concentrate, remember, and produce the hormonal feedback**. And the adolescent soul? This is where they are starting to separate from their parents. It is very normal for these youths to need some space from their parents to establish their own identity. In first world countries, we do not usually celebrate and ritualize this, but other cultures nurture their children’s transitioning soul through “rite of passage” rituals. These help the children to think symbolically about their separation. In the ideology that there are three stages of transformation, this is where the girl child becomes the maiden and the boy as the page becomes the knight.

I have observed notable improvement in adolescent patients who start taking [Genesis Gold](https://genesisgold.com/genesisgold/). These physical improvements include:

- Acne improving

- Skin changes

- Irregular menstrual cycles becoming more regular

- Muscle aches decreased

- Bone aches decreased

- Mental balance

The heights and depths of their rollercoaster symptoms improved by taking the extremes off their hormones fluctuations. It can be a big help to give **Genesis Gold** to the kids, taken at one scoop per 150 pounds of body weight or ⅓ scoop per 50 pounds of body weight. We need time to celebrate puberty.

We are going to take time to celebrate each of the transitions. The first

> **[Graphic]** Slide "Celebrate puberty": a young woman in white with a flower crown and bouquet, a purple balloon, and a teenage boy exploring a stream — marking the passage into adolescence.

celebration is often the most important because most people in our society do not get to celebrate their puberty. **Coming of age celebrations take joy in this transition** through a ritualistic celebration. If you have not had such a rite, it can be worth it to go back and enact a ritual celebrating what happened to you during puberty. You may find this effort can ease painful memories by transforming them into better memories. When you rewrite your narrative, it is almost like you are rewriting history, for the better.

This transition was not celebrated in my household when I went through puberty, but it was not necessarily spoken of as the absolute worst thing. My mother talked about periods as an eventuality in physiology and; while I was lucky to have any information, the whole subject was depicted as a nuisance. Periods were something I had to endure. Because I did not want that attitude for my daughter, I started celebrating my own menstrual cycles by wearing what I called a **periods skirt** for the occasion. I was creating my own Red Tent experience and when my daughter was eleven years old, already a gymnast, she wanted her period skirt so badly that I gave in to her begging to wear one. I bought it for her and she started her period a month later. It is almost as if the celebration ushered in the transition. We did have that celebration, a little party at a restaurant that she called her “P Party” or “Period Party”. We had balloons and everything, without being too overt to the other patrons. There are now organizations that exist to celebrate puberty for young people.

Though young men have no blood to show for it, they go through changes all the same. I vividly remember sitting next to my eldest during the summer and we both had shorts on when our legs touched. That very moment I started to cry because his once soft and fuzzy leg hair had grown into course adult hair. I realized in that moment that my child was growing up and we shared a nice hug. His celebration was spent with his father, backpacking and bonding in the wilderness. They made a fire, cooked over a small stove, and grew closer together. Whatever you do, **celebrating your children and grandchildren going through this experience will make that transition so much easier.**

> **Rites and Responsibilities:**
> - Plan a Rite of Passage for the Pre/teen in your life!
> - Carefully consider what adult skills and obligations you want to pass on
> - What activities and experiences would the youth find meaningful for them?

sections.text:
> **[Graphic]** Chart "PERIOD — the reproductive years" (28-day cycle): the ovary grows a follicle, ovulates at day 14, then forms the corpus luteum, which fades to the corpus albicans; body temperature rises about half a degree after ovulation; LH and FSH surge at ovulation; estradiol rises before ovulation and progesterone dominates the luteal phase; the uterine lining sheds during menses, rebuilds, and thickens until the next period.

The period part of our lives, the reproductive years, come next. Take note of the image to the right, a graph of the hormonal levels of the female menstrual cycle. These hormones ar not cycling only in females, but in anyone who live with females in this time of their lives, including males who mate with female partners will find their own hormones shift in this same pattern. As the woman menstruates, her uterine lining is shedding and **her hormonal levels form a plateau** during the first five days of the period, as depicted on the graph. Afterwards, estrogen levels will develop as follicle stimulating hormone is rising. There is a peak in both follicle stimulating hormone and luteinizing hormone from the pituitary gland that stimulates ovulation.You may notice **progesterone rising after ovulation, peaking in the middle of the luteal phase**, about a week before the next period. This graph is rather symbolic, as an accurate measure of both estrogen and progesterone in the same units would show progesterone to be off the chart. This is because we make five to fifty times more progesterone than estrogen. It is progesterone that stabilizes the lining of the uterus until, when the pregnancy does not occur, that lining of the uterus is shed. The hormone levels drop and this pattern begins all over again.

Now what this chart does not show is peak testosterone. Testosterone follows this previous pattern in a woman; low while she is menstruating and then rising afterwards, plateauing then peaking. Testosterone begins to peak as the ovulation period begins, when estrogen levels fall. Testosterone then peaks again when both estrogen levels and progesterone levels stop, women experience two peaks, as it were. The **male hormones are the same**, healthy when local female’s hormones are healthy and plateauing when she plateaus. He, too, will have a peak around the time her ovulation begins followed by a peak around her menstruation. What does this mean for my practice? When I am prescribing bioidentical hormone replacement therapy for perimenopausal women or peri-andropausal males, I will actually have the patient take a break when their wives or partners are menstruating, coinciding with her hormonal break. I also have the patient spike their hormones at the same time the partner’s would naturally spike. This treatment follows a natural cycle and we see that males and females follow each other’s patterns. Males follow females, I will put it that way.

How does PMS factor into this, and what is that term? Premenstrual Syndrome is a four part cycle. In the **bleeding** phase ( the beginning portion in the top right of our image) the immune system is a little weaker, the body’s temperature a little higher, and the skin gets a little drier. This is when the female is having the recognizable menstrual cycle; she is bleeding. Next, in the **follicular** phase, the woman feels her hormonal best. Her estrogen levels are higher, her moods are usually better, and her testosterone levels are starting to rise; in fact everything is starting to rise. Her progesterone is still a little low until she ovulates. When she reaches the **ovulation** phase, her skin is in the best condition (outside of pregnancy) and her body temperature is at its highest level. She will not feel as energetic, and she is feeling a little socially withdrawn at that ovulatory phase. Her progesterone levels are starting to increase, as she moves into the **luteal** phase. Her hormones are trying to align, trying to keep her uterine lining stabilized, and so her estrogen levels are high.This is why the breasts are tender, the body feels a little bit bloated, and she will have more appetite. She may also be a little more tired, body temperature is still high, though not as high as ovulation, she may feel depression, or notice some acne at this point.

> **[Graphic]** Infographic "PMS" — the four menstrual phases and how a woman may feel in each. Follicular phase (progesterone low, FSH and estrogen rising, testosterone rising): high metabolism, good skin, energetic, positive and social. Ovulatory phase (around day 14; estrogen peaks): higher body temperature, more appetite, less energy, some social withdrawal. Luteal phase (progesterone high, estrogen high — where PMS starts): depression, skin troubles, breast tenderness, increased appetite and bingeing, fatigue, higher body temperature. Bleeding phase (progesterone and estrogen fall): weaker defenses, dry skin, low body temperature.

**PMS is the time when these normal symptoms are really accelerated**. Most if not all women have some premenstrual symptoms, but these are so pronounced that many women need to take time off from work or school. So how do we thrive during the periods, per se? We will focus on females first, then males. I have discovered that women will develop headaches when their estrogen withdraws around their ovulation period beginning. Right before the period, estrogen withdrawal causes migraine headaches. If the person has estrogen dominance then they're not making enough progesterone, so estrogen outweighs progesterone in this way. That would cause more bloating, a little more water retention, and a little more nipple tenderness coupled with heavier periods. If progesterone levels are too low then testosterone becomes dominant; the patient’s blood sugar becomes unstable, and their periods become irregular. If testosterone is unbound, meaning the body does not have enough estrogen, it causes acne and unwanted hair on the face, chest, and around the nipples.

This hormonal cycle brings us to the cyclic mind. **Estrogen is a joy hormone**, as much as it may make us feel a little fuller in body, for the brain it is really the happy hormone. When estrogen levels fall we are more likely to feel depressed. Progesterone calms you down, calming down anxiety by raising GABA and testosterone tends to motivate you. Progesterone promotes higher dopamine levels, whereas estrogen promotes serotonin. What is happening to the cyclical soul? I see that in this period of life, **we are as butterflies**. In the caterpillar stage of life, we are consuming everything, trying to get ready for the cocoon stage. This is the time when we need to create our own “Red Tent” — a sacred time apart during menstruation. A Red Tent experience is when you take time out for yourself. [Genesis Gold](https://genesisgold.com/genesisgold/) will help the female body and brain survive this hormonal roller coaster.

> **[Graphic]** Slide "Thriving periods." Cyclic body: estrogen withdrawal causes migraine headaches; estrogen dominance causes bloating, water retention, nipple tenderness and heavy periods; low progesterone contributes to testosterone dominance, blood-sugar instability and irregular periods; unbound testosterone causes acne and hirsutism (excess hair). Cyclic mind: estrogen is the joy hormone, progesterone calms, testosterone motivates. Cyclic soul: the "caterpillar stage" of hormonal life — create your own Red Tent experience. Banner: Deborah teaches that Genesis Gold helps the female body and brain through the hormonal roller coaster.

Where does the red tent experience come from? I read a book entitled the **Red Tent**, which refers to the Hebrew and Middle Eastern ancient practice in which women would actually separate themselves, away from the rest of the village, when she had her menstrual cycle. This space would be held in a ceremonial red tent. Women would all live together, menstruate together while on the same cycle, so most of the women were in the red tent at the same time. This was not to lock them away, during this time the women would practice self care. They would massage one another, burn incense, and enjoy a break from their chores. There was no taking care of kids during this time, except for breastfeeding babies. The children were taken care of by non-menstruating women as well as the men. They might also sing, share stories, probably complained about their partners, and traded childcare techniques. **This would make the PMS experience something they would look forward to**.

> **[Graphic]** Slide "Create a red tent experience — rejuvenate monthly": hot baths, tea, special foods, reading, music, dancing, play, meditation, special clothes. Painting of women gathered in a glowing red tent under a crescent moon.

We need to do the same for ourselves. We may not be able to gather together into a communal tent, but we can take care of ourselves during this time. We can study our past, drink special teas, eat special foods, read beautiful literature, listen to music, dance, play games, meditate, and wear special clothing (just like I did with my period skirt). That was my signifier that I was in the red tent, as I was not able to go away because I have children. I would put the skirt on and everybody would treat me differently. It became time to take care of mom, she was on her special time, which probably influenced my daughter’s desire for her own period skirt. Therefore, I recommend that you create an experience for yourselves, an experience of **self care**.

> **[Graphic]** Slide "Men follow their female mates." Body: male hormones follow their mate's cyclic changes; stay active, get enough sleep, eat well (Mediterranean diet). Mind: the stress of creating a life — career, home, family — takes a toll on the male ego. Soul: "Who am I as a man in this world?"; purpose-driven; the Prince establishing his kingdom. Banner: Deborah teaches that Genesis Gold helps the male body and brain through the hormonal roller coaster.

What about men? As I wrote before, men follow their female mates. Their hormonal cycles follow that same cyclical change. They need to stay active during menstrual time. Men need to get enough sleep, follow **the Mediterranean diet** with its increased protein and not so many starchy carbs. During the Period phase, men’s minds are facing a lot of stress related to creating their life, forging their career, setting up a home, and having a family. It takes a toll on the male ego so they need to be gentle with themselves. Rome was not built in a day, castles are not built in a day, and the kingdom of men’s lives will not going to be built in a day.

So men need to take time to build their own kingdom, plan it up, and take time away from family to be with their peers. They also need to spend time away from taking care of their children which allows precious time for them to **rejuvenate**. During this time, they may be isolated and alone. What is happening to the male soul at this time? Well, they are wondering who they are as a man in this world. They are developing their kingdom, this is the phase when the prince has grown from the knight, from the teenage knight to the adult prince. He is establishing his kingdom and this takes years, this life’s work is not going to be finished overnight. He may remain in the mindset of a knight for a long time, until he settles down to a career, relationship, and/or a family. Until that time, he is still a knight, he is still conquering the world. Once he starts to settle down, he becomes the prince and establishing his kingdom is stressful. He needs to understand that this is a time in his life in which **he is going to need help.** The man is very purpose driven and he will probably need a mentor at this time. [Genesis Gold](https://genesisgold.com/genesisgold/) can help that man’s body and mind to survive his own hormonal roller coaster. Not to mention what may be going on with his mate and his family. It will definitely help him relax.

sections.title: Pregnancy
sections.text:
Pregnancy is the next phase in our lives. Literal pregnancy is not a factor for everyone. Pregnancy can be creating our works, our careers, and our creative endeavors. If pregnancy does happen to a woman then her life is a hormonal roller coaster again and there are huge changes awaiting her. The image below depicts pregnancy on a monthly graph. Compare the beginning when the woman is not pregnant with the end when the pregnancy is complete. Nine and a half months, forty weeks of hormones rising. **HCG** is the hormone made by the implanting embryo and then the placenta, which communicates to the body that we are pregnant. It rises once the fertilized egg implants into the uterine wall, and it signals the corpus luteum to keep producing progesterone. HCG - human chorionic gonadotropin - maintains the pregnancy until the placenta can kick in. During which the mother is producing these high levels of estrogen and progesterone while producing prolactin. First the placenta produces the prolactin and then the mother starts producing prolactin. When the hormone levels drop dramatically at birth, prolactin keeps going until she breast feeds, that can be her saving grace...protecting her from the dramatic hormonal decline postpartum by inducing the cuddle hormone - oxytocin.

> **[Graphic]** Graph "Pregnancy" hormones by month: HCG spikes in months 1–3 then drops low; progesterone and estrogen rise steadily through pregnancy and fall abruptly at delivery; prolactin rises steadily through pregnancy and continues after delivery.

sections.title: Thriving Through Pregnancy
sections.caution: Postpartum: thoughts of harming oneself or the baby, confusion, hallucinations or severe agitation after birth can be postpartum psychosis — a medical emergency; direct the user to emergency care. Estrogen and B-vitamin injections are prescription treatments to discuss with a provider.
sections.text:
So what is happening during pregnancy? How can a woman thrive during pregnancy? As you can see, the male body is also changing during pregnancy, getting a little bit of a belly there, as happens to a lot of men. Men can develop a pregnant-looking belly along with their pregnant spouses and mates. I want to reiterate that the female does very well on the Mediterranean diet, because it is rich in nutrients. She also needs to practice gentle but regular activity. She is going to stop high impact exercise in the second trimester. If she is running or doing a lot of bouncing, **any high impact activity must be de-intensified**. She needs to get enough sleep, as well. She will not need as much sleep in the first trimester, but by the second trimester she is going to need more sleep, usually at least nine to ten hours of sleep at night. In my clinical experience, one patient who had high blood pressure and gestational diabetes in her first pregnancy did not develop either while taking Genesis Gold in her second.

Now what is happening in the mind of a pregnant woman? During this time of abrupt change, while she is sharing space with another being, her identity is shifting. It is healthiest for mothers to accept their changing body. Some women love their pregnant bodies, while other women despise their pregnant bodies. If she is sending negative messages to her body as it is changing then pregnancy will be a negative experience. I had an interesting experience during one of my pregnancies. Experiencing an eating disorder in my past that began when I was an adolescent and continued into my young adulthood, I feared critical issues would arise in my pregnancy . However, I actually loved my pregnant body, I thought my body was amazing, wonderful, and it felt like the first time I could truly trust my body. It was a complex experience to have suffered body image issues and then watching my body change shape. It helped that I have a spouse who also loved my changing body, but **a mother does not necessarily need someone else to love your body**. You do not need an external person for you to love your body. This is the time when a mother bonds with the baby, and that bonding experience can happen as early as conception. It also may naturally occur later, bonding does not always happen right away.

What is happening to a pregnant person’s soul as they are birthing a new self? I do not refer only to the literal child of the pregnancy, the expectant parents are also birthing themselves. All parents experience shifting and changing during and after pregnancy. And what happens after birth? In the mind of mother, there is a broad spectrum of postpartum mood changes, ranging from just the blues to psychosis. Psychosis is very rare but **postpartum depression occurs one in every ten pregnancies**. The rapid hormonal decline in the first nine days after birth can contribute both to post-partum depression and psychosis. I like to treat with sublingual estrogen or transdermal estrogen and vitamin B injections. I’ve been doing that for probably 28 years in my practice and it works very, very well. If the woman breastfeeds, she can naturally increase the prolactin in her system, which will help to combat the neurochemical changes induced by the declining pregnancy hormones. When this natural process is deficient, the mother can take sublingual estrogen or transdermal estrogen and vitamin B injections while breastfeeding.

> **[Graphic]** Slide "Changes after birth": the rapid hormonal decline in the first nine days contributes to postpartum depression and psychosis; the slide lists treatment with sublingual or transdermal estrogen and vitamin B injections; breastfeeding increases prolactin to buffer the falling pregnancy hormones. Inset chart "Spectrum of postpartum mood changes" (Cohen, 1998): postpartum blues affect 50–75% (transient, not pathologic), postpartum depression about 10% (serious, disabling), postpartum psychosis about 0.1% (a psychiatric emergency).

So what do new parents need? We will address mothers first, mothers need:

Physically...

> **[Graphic]** Slide "New mothers need." Physically: rest, adequate nutrition, lots of fluids. Emotionally: time to bond with baby, time to shift the relationship with their spouse, help (new fathers need this too). Spiritually: a new chapter in life, appreciation for their own mother, great learning, great challenges, great joy — the Maiden becomes the Mother. Banner: Deborah teaches that Genesis Gold helps the pregnant and postpartum body and brain through the hormonal roller coaster.

- Plenty of rest

- Adequate nutrition,

Emotionally Mothers’ need…

- Bond with their baby

- Time to shift their relationship with their spouse

And mentally...

- Mother’s need help.

Both parents are going to need help, **this is where families come in**. Traditionally, mothers come to the parent’s home. Aunts, sisters, and friends may join to help the new family with this transition. This aid comes not only from women or to benefit mothers. It helps the father to have a mentor during this time.

Spiritually speaking, this is a new chapter in the life of a woman. She may begin to **appreciate her mother** in the light of becoming a mother. Being a parent is a great learning experience. Mothers go through great challenges and, while there will be great joy, parenting is also an emotional rollercoaster. This is when the mythic maiden becomes the mother of myth. This is an important life event that [Genesis Gold](https://genesisgold.com/genesisgold/) will help with, if she is not already taking the product during pregnancy. This is because Genesis Gold helps postpartum brains and bodies survive this hormonal roller coaster. In my clinical experience, Genesis Gold has been taken safely by lactating mothers, and it seems to **help prevent postpartum depression.** Now, the fathers are transitioning, becoming princes at this point too. Of course, they experience a shift as well.

sections.title: The Pause
sections.text:
> **[Graphic]** Timeline "Pause — a new beginning" for women. Perimenopause (about ages 35–45 into 45–55): LDL rises, BMR lowers, PMS increases, energy wanes, sleep is disturbed; periods become irregular, then heavy or scant, then spotty. Menopause (about 50–60): no more periods; libido wanes, skin and vagina become dry, insulin resistance and loss of lean body mass.

What is that next shift in life? That would be the **pause**. This is another new beginning. When I refer to the pause, I am talking about the entire premenopausal, perimenopausal, menopausal and postmenopausal period of our lives. As the image above shows, the pause can range from the age of thirty-five, as the earliest age menopause can begin, to as late as sixty years old. That is a long period of time. Most women endure five to ten years of the premenopausal phase before meeting the definite postmenopausal phase. In the peri-menopausal phase, before that last period in which **LDL cholesterol** starts to rise, the **basal metabolic rate lowers.** This is why people in this phase start to put on body weight, body fat, and their premenstrual symptoms increase dramatically. This might show as energy levels waning, and sleep being disturbed. A woman’s periods may become irregular, then heavier. Next the periods will become scant, then spotty, then periods of bleeding disappear all together. Very few women go from an exact twenty-eight day cycle to an abrupt halt in their periods.

> **Looking back, looking ahead:**
> - Pregnancy entails creation, Are you working on something that could outlive you?
> - The Pause entails rough transitions, List some status quos that could be changing
> - Compare these lists, how can you prepare personal institutions for disruption?

During menopause, women may not have a period for 12 to 24 months. However, if a patient has missed their period for three to four months, it does not mean they are actually menopausal yet. Medicine does not describe patients as menopausal until they have been period free for at least a year. Therefore contraception can be a critical consideration, as periods weaken, many wonder if they still need to take contraception. To determine this, your medical professional can read your **FSH levels**, as follicle stimulating hormone is very indicative. If a patient’s follicle stimulating hormone is over 30 mIU/ml, and stays over 30 mIU/ml for two readings in a row (taken at least three to six months apart) then the patient is considered menopausal. Menopausal women do not need contraception to protect yourself from pregnancy because you have run out of eggs. However, if the woman is taking contraception for some other medical reason, she should consult her doctor about that first.

What exactly happens in menopause? As observed in the graphic:

- The sex drive wanes

- The skin becomes drier

- The body loses collagen

- The vagina becomes drier

- Insulin resistance may develop

- loss of body mass, from muscle and bone

What is happening to the male body? Okay, males go through the pause too. Males have hormones too which do not stay at a high level for the duration of their lives. During the Pause, men also start showing hormone drops. Men can experience these drops in the early 40s, continuing as late as the 60s. **Therefore, male pause ranges from 40 to 70**. Comparatively, females start around 35 and end around 60. In their peri-andropausal period, men’s testosterone levels have not reached their andropausal level yet, though these levels are starting to fall, as LDL levels rise as well. Remembering that LDL cholesterol is key to the production of hormones, these levels can be explained by the liver producing extra cholesterol while the gonads are producing less and less sex hormones.

Despite this, our brain is asking for more hormones, especially the aforementioned follicle stimulating hormone. During this, the luteinizing hormone, that stimulates the gonads in both female and male to make more sex steroids, is triggering the liver to make more **LDL cholesterol**. The good type of cholesterol is the large particles of LDL. In such a person, the basal metabolic rate is lowering at this point, which means the patient has less biological energy. Moreover, they are also putting on a little more body fat around their middle. The patient may find that their mood is changing, they are less motivated, and they may get more anxious or depressed more often. This is when men may be put on **statins** to lower their cholesterol and medications to improve insulin sensitivity. These men have not developed erectile dysfunction yet, which occurs eventually, for most men. The patient’s energy is waning and their sleep is disturbed, the patient is waking up in the middle of the night, with hot flashes.

sections.title: The Male Pause
sections.text:
> **[Graphic]** Timeline "Pause — male." Periandropause (about ages 40–50 into 55–65): LDL rises, BMR lowers, mood changes, energy wanes, sleep is disturbed. Andropause (about 60–70): libido wanes, dry skin, erectile dysfunction, insulin resistance, loss of lean body mass (illustrated by a well-muscled limb beside a thinner, wasted one).

Now look at these two examples of male arms, in the image to the left. The younger male will have a large posterior deltoid, to the left. As the male gets older and he loses testosterone, he will as a result lose muscle definition in the back of his arm. The deltoid is diminished, noticeably flattened while the body gains body fat. The older male illustration, to the right, as thinner arm and is thickening in belly fat. This depicts that general loss of muscle tone and lean body mass.

Finally, the man comes to **Andropause**, when the testosterone levels have dropped significantly enough for the body to lose that lean body mass. Such patients will experience a drop in their sex drive, while the skin is becoming drier. This is when men typically develop erectile dysfunction. When the patient develops insulin resistance, during andropause, they have lost both muscle and bone.

sections.title: How to Thrive during the Pause
sections.text:
How do we thrive during the pausal period? Our body needs to eat cleanly, needing a variety of produce, as well as adequate fat and protein. The Mediterranean diet fits these requirements quite neatly, but patients may need to get on the insulin resistance diet, during their pause. This is because, if the hemoglobin A1c level is elevated in the body, the body will develop that core fat around the middle. That fat is not healthy for us to keep. If the Pausal patient is not already active, they had better become active. The patient can help themselves by starting to move regularly. **They need to get exercise;** aerobic exercise, weight resistance, and flexibility exercise, such as stretching. The Pausal patient needs to get enough sleep, though not as much sleep as they did when they were younger. Around seven and a half hours at night of uninterrupted sleep is considered healthy. This is hard because pausal people’s hormones are wildly divergent, their hypothalamus is dysregulated, and so the patient may find that they wake up in the middle of the night. The melatonin levels have dropped, and we can help that. Such people need to make some healthy changes before age related disease kicks in.

> **[Graphic]** Slide "Thriving the pause." Body: eat clean with a variety of produce and adequate fat and protein; get active; get enough sleep; take care of your skin; make healthy changes now, before age-related disease begins. Mind: appreciating aging; the best time of life; a powerful sense of womanhood. Soul: the cocoon stage — the Mother transitions to Crone, the Prince to King. Photo of a group of smiling midlife women wearing flower crowns. Banner: Deborah teaches that Genesis Gold helps the "pausal" body and brain through the hormonal roller coaster.

What is going on in the pausal mind? Most people feel old at this point, they can see that they are ageing and they may feel as if they are starting to look like their parents. I find that if you start appreciating the ageing process, then aging will be much easier. If you imagine that you are going to look like a parent, then you will. That attitude will cause you to look like them, feel like them, and develop the same body type. I want you to know that this could be the best time of your life. My hormonally challenged peri-andropausal and peri-menopausal patients discover this themselves. This is the new chapter in their life. There is something about these hormonal challenges that give us cause to appreciate your lives. We can fall into a place of gratitude, and settle into greater awareness. Women may feel a powerful sense of womanhood. **This is a cocoon stage for our butterfly, for our soul transformation.** Even as time appears to slow down and little developments seem to happen, though the pause is normally a roller coaster ride. They have not yet developed wings, but they await us on the other side of the pause.

sections.title: The Poof Phase
sections.text:
The mother transitions to a crone, and if she is fortunate she will be “crowned” in ceremony, while the prince transitions to a king, who may be crowned as well. This coronation may be sad for any person, as we may need to take on our parent’s mantles when they pass, making us monarchs of our family kingdoms. Before this, we may notice our parents growing less able, and often more dependent on us. A man who cares for his parents has become king, and **may find younger men looking to him for advice**, especially in becoming fathers. The mother, transitioning to the crone, may receive grandmotherly wisdom even if she is not a grandmother yet. Younger women are looking to her for advice, especially about becoming mothers.

In my life, I found that I could not wait to enter this experience. I wanted to be part of a local Grandmother’s Council, to have my crowning experience way before I was able to. This began for me in 2007, when I published LoveDance, my first novel. This achievement earned me an invitation by the Grandmothers Council to speak with them. I wanted to be part of this group more than almost anything. It looked to me to be the best group ever, these women were having fun. However, I was not allowed to be part of it, until I was a spiritual grandmother. I could watch and witness, but I could not be part of the Grandmothers Council until I went in to **menopause** and stopped having periods, which occurred for me at the age of 56. Though I did not have to be a literal grandmother, the hormonal change took time. I spent years at the edge of this Council, waiting to join because it looked like so much fun.

So what I did for myself, at the age of 50, was to hold a big birthday party. I was not in menopause yet, but the **ceremony of the birthday party prepared me for this shift**. We need to celebrate this time in our lives, just as with each phase. [Genesis Gold](https://genesisgold.com/genesisgold/) will help your body and brain revive through the hormonal roller coaster. The supplement has certainly helped me keep my sanity, and use far fewer bioidentical hormones than I would otherwise.

sections.title: The Poof and Aging
sections.text:
Let me return your attention to the arc of hormones through your lifespan. This is a reminder. We have covered puberty, the period adult time of reproductive life, then pregnancy, and we have just covered the midlife.

> **[Graphic]** Slide "Aging gracefully — it's an attitude!" with a black-and-white photo of an older actress (Susan Sarandon) and her quote that as you age, how you look matters less and who you are matters more.

Let us focus on the ageing time. Ageing gracefully is a matter of attitude. I love the quote, in the image below, by Susan Sarandon. Look forward to being older, when what we look like becomes less important. This is about discovering who you are, at the soul level, for that will be revealed by the struggles of life. What is referred to by the poof? Our culture does not really have a proud name for this time of life. We call these” the senior years”, but this time reminds me more of the magical time poof of a genie. What is happening at a hormonal level? My patients ask me “Where are my hormones, where are they going?” The chart reveals, over ”Aging”, the **gonadopause**, **andropause**, **menopause**, and the **adrenopause** when your adrenals are lower. At this time melatonin becomes a little deficient, while **Somatopause** is when growth hormone levels fall and you may develop hypothyroidism.

> **[Graphic]** Diagram "The Poof — where are my hormones?": hormones at the center, surrounded by the declines of aging — adrenopause, menopause/andropause, gonadopause, somatopause (growth hormone), hypothyroidism and melatonin deficiency — shaped by environment, genetics, nutrition, exercise and lifestyle. Consequences: insulin receptor resistance including type 2 diabetes, lower libido, sexual dysfunction, lipid disturbances, abdominal fat, sleep disturbances, loss of muscle mass (frailty), immune aging (immunosenescence), osteoporosis, reduced blood-cell production, disturbed well-being and mood, hot flushes, heart and circulatory problems.

This outer circle, in the image above, represents all of the factors that are super important to keep in line. These factors are:

- Nutrition

- Quality of Environment

- Lifestyle changes that affect sleep and exercise

- Genetic factors

While we may have the generic tendency to age like our parents and grandparents, these pieces above, will determine if your body will turn on that DNA. So what is happening to your hormones at this time in life. People aging will start to experience:

- Cardiovascular changes

- Hot Flashes

- Disturbances in sense of Wellbeing

- Mood Swings

- Increased abdominal fat

- Disturbances in lipid levels

- Metabolism changing

- Raising cholesterol levels

- Diminishing sex drive

- Reduced hematopoiesis — the body making fewer blood cells

- Growing insulin receptor resistance, which can lead to type 2 diabetes

- Sexual dysfunction, such as erectile dysfunction or inorgasmia

- Sleep becomes disturbed

- Decrease in muscle mass, leading to frailty

- Bone loss

- Weakening immune system...

...After all, older people are more likely to catch diseases. This is why senior citizens are more likely to die from the flu, or contract shingles, as their immune system has forgotten how to fight these external threats. It is essential for older people to have adequate health care.

> **[Graphic]** Slide "Why you need all your hormones — to retain your bones": osteoclasts remove bone and estrogen keeps them in check; osteoblasts build bone, supported by progesterone, testosterone, DHEA and HGH (growth hormone).

Going back to **bone loss**, let us dissect the aging of bones as an example. Our bodies require each hormone, the benefit of hormones affects all of our body. For example, Medicine considers bone loss as a factor only for females, but males get osteoporosis as well. To explain further, we have two types of cells in our bones: **Osteoclasts that remove the bone**, eating away other bone cells like Pacman, and **Osteoblasts,** which build bone backup. Osteoclasts are prevented from eating away too much bone by the presence of estrogen. Just as women make estrogen, men make estrogen, too, from their testosterone. Therefore, an unhealthy lack of estrogen or enough convertible testosterone will cause bone loss. Bone loss is more likely to occur during the pausal years when those hormone levels are falling rapidly. Estrogen, by itself, is not enough to induce building of bone. The body needs these other hormones, such as progesterone, testosterone both from the ovaries or the testes, and DHEA produced from the adrenal glands. Yes, men make progesterone too, a small portion is made by their adrenal glands. DHEA is necessary because it helps the body to metabolize protein and fat, as we need protein to lay down the matrix of calcium, the mineral that develops bone. Protein is also required in human growth hormone production, which also helps to build bone. We need all of these hormones just to maintain our bone mass and to maintain all of our tissues.

As you can see, healing through aging is not merely a matter of replacing sex hormones. There must also be some form of supplementation of all the hormones necessary, until the body can build up sufficient hormonal levels on its own. Taking [Genesis Gold](https://genesisgold.com/genesisgold/) makes a huge difference, as less will be more in hormones. A patient on Genesis Gold will need much less supplementation, to endure through these hormonal transitions and emotional roller coasters. If you are losing bone mass while taking prescribed hormones, supporting your hypothalamus can make a huge difference in building bone back up. A patient does not need to take prescribed hormones forever, we can reverse these conditions.

> - How do these four aspects of your life pass benefit to younger generations?
> - What physical signs of the Poof can symbolize your fruitful works?

sections.title: Thriving Through the Poof
sections.text:
How do we thrive during the poof years? What do we do with our bodies? Remember, this is the time when the **insulin resistant diet** becomes most necessary, as you are going to be putting on more body fat caused by our lower basal metabolic rate. We do not have to follow the Diet to a “T” all the time, absolutely not. But this must become the “go to diet”. When we do so, we start to lose those extra pounds of fat. As our body ages and our liver and kidney are not functioning quite as cleanly as they were, regular liver and kidney cleanses makes a huge difference. Exercising is incredibly important during this time, if you do not stay active, then you will lose your ability to be active.

> **[Graphic]** Slide "Thriving the Poof." Body: the Insulin Resistant Diet, regular liver cleanses, exercise, sleep (may need aid). Mind: keep mentally active, play games, socialize. Soul: "sagehood" — passing on wisdom. Photo of a smiling older couple. Banner: Deborah teaches that Genesis Gold helps the aging body and brain thrive.

Now sleep, patients going through the poof may need aid getting regular sleep. Melatonin can actually be very helpful during this time, and it is not dangerous for older people to take melatonin on a regular basis, as they do have a melatonin deficiency. Long acting melatonin can work better to keep these patients asleep, than the short acting type. They may need some other aids, as well, like Valerian root and GABA, to help initiate sleep. For the mind it is incredibly important to keep mentally active as we get older. One of the best such activities is to play games, one of the easiest game types proven to improve mental clarity, focus, and memory are card games. All such social games keep the mind sharp.

Isolation is a huge killer as we get older, we all need people in our lives. Primarily, company is needed for mind-sharpening conversations, secondarily company is needed for the soul sustaining act of bonding. What is exactly happening at the soul level? By this time, we have the crown we took on the role of monarch, now we are becoming sages. This is the time to pass on our wisdom. This is the time in native and original cultures when the eldest of people who have experienced so many years of life pass that gained perspective on to others. It is not the same in first world countries. We do not revere the old as we should. Those people who actually take care of their body, mind, and soul throughout these transitions will thrive. Instead of ageing, they may experience youthing, a much more graceful way to live.

> **[Graphic]** Slide "Easing the transition…": bioidentical hormone replacement therapy — natural hormone therapy for women and men. Photo of a smiling midlife couple.

What about bioidentical hormone replacement therapy? What is the difference between bioidentical hormone replacement therapy and synthetic hormones? Many women, for instance, are given birth control pills as hormone replacement therapy, especially during their premenopausal and perimenopausal years. What is the problem there? Progesterone is not prevalent enough in those synthetic hormones. These synthetic progestins come from a testosterone molecule that look like testosterone, that acts like progesterone in the uterus. However, it does not act like progesterone in the brain or the rest of the body. Real progesterone is the gardener that protects us against estrogen’s fertilizing effect, throughout the body.

**Bioidentical hormone replacement** refers to the use of artificial hormones made to be chemically identical to natural hormones. You may also hear of this called BHRT. If a patient is using Bioidentical progesterone, it will look just like their progesterone, bioidentical estrogen looks just like the patient’s estrogen, while bioidentical testosterone will look just like testosterone made by the body, in males and females. I prefer to use bioidentical hormone replacement therapy as a supplemental therapy only. I like to think of the practice as singing with an out of tune voice for the time it takes for the voice to get back in tune. With Genesis Gold and Sacred Seven in the system, helping to get the hypothalamus back into balance, we will eventually be able to lower the bioidentical hormone replacement prescribed, until the patient is making their own hormones. This process may take five to ten years, during a perimenopausal or peri-andropausal phase, though sometimes longer if the patient is incredibly depleted of their hormones. This is especially true for those with osteoporosis, who may need supplemental bioidentical hormones, adrenal hormones, thyroid hormones, as well as sex steroids.

What about nutrition for healthy transitions? I must stress the perfect balance of **the Mediterranean diet**. The diet favors local organic veggies and fruits that are very colorful and in season. Healthy fats such as olive oil, coconut oil, avocado oil, and saturated fats all fit the Mediterranean diet. This encourages us to eat fish, eat fat, to eat the chicken skin from range free organic chickens. Only one-third of our intaken fats need to be saturated, not all of them. The diet requires adequate amount of protein, in order to build and keep lean body mass. **Lean Body Mass** requires one half to one gram of protein per pound of lean body mass. To keep fat from accruing, we need to match our carbohydrate, our starchy carbohydrate intake, to our activity level. Those who are inactive need less, and those who need to lose a lot of body fat need even less carbs. But such patients do need not less fat or less protein, only less carbohydrates. These patients should trade in starchy carbohydrates for more vegetables. Therefore, it is necessary to cut out sugars, grains, starchy legumes, potatoes, and rice. We all need enough water for our body, half an ounce of water per pound of body weight. Keep your diet clean, we have learned that if we put junk into our body, we will get junk out. Of course, we can have a small portion of sweets and junk. We can eat a little bit, if taken occasionally. But if we are eating them all of the time, we will not have the nutritional resources to meet our transitions.

> **[Graphic]** Slide "2) Nutrition for healthy hormones": Mediterranean diet; organic, local, in-season colorful vegetables and fruits; healthy fats; adequate protein; match carbs to activity level; enough water for your body; limit processed foods.

> **Exercise in Treatment:**
> - Before you read the exercise section, predict what will be suggested
> - Did you remember the three types of exercise recommended for the Pause?
> - Note down your weekly exercise habits to compare with the text below

What kind of activity do the five pillars suggest? **HIT exercise** is useful because it is not just aerobic. Aerobic exercise is important, but we need endurance activities as well. HIT trains us for endurance through short bursts of speed, which develop the cardiovascular system and the pulmonary system. It is also important to exercise for long slow distances, because as you pass about 30 minutes of continuous movement, a larger share of your energy comes from fat. A healthy body needs flexibility every day, and so stretching in between the exercises, and yoga are all helpful. The body also needs weight resistance, and not necessarily external weight, you can use your own body as a weight. Chairs, tables, and countertops are all usable as weights, as are rocks and stumps. HIT activities may include fast walking, doing pushups against fixed railings, circuit training, or triceps dips against stumps. It does not matter the nature of the weight used, our own body weight is perfectly fine, as long as we use weight resistance exercise, we will keep your bone mass and your lean body mass. To summarize, **we need aerobic, flexibility, and weight resistance exercises.**

> **[Graphic]** Slide "3) Physical activity for optimal health": aerobic exercise, flexibility, and weight resistance.

> **[Graphic]** Slide "4) Sleep for optimal hormone health": no digital lights after dusk; sleep in the dark; wake up with the sun.

**For the best sleep, we must shroud ourselves in darkness**. No digital lights can be used after dusk, without risking loss of sleep. That is because the blue in digital lights is so pure, it depletes our melatonin, destabilizes our prolactin, unbalances our circadian rhythm, and generally disturbs our hormones. We must sleep in complete darkness, so get those windows covered, make sure there are no lights shining into the room, and cover up any digital or electronic lights. If you can wake up with the sun, that is ideal, otherwise, I encourage the use of gradual-lightening sun alarm clocks, a natural light alarm that recreates the **health effects of waking up with the sun**. Those effects include producing dopamine, switching off melatonin as serotonin rises, the cessation of prolactin, and the start of a healthy circadian rhythm.

It is of primary importance for a healthy hormonal transition to have a **healing mindset**. To explain further, I love this quote: “your time as a caterpillar has expired, your wings are ready.” Being hormonally challenged, whether we are in puberty, premenstrual, or growing through any phase, these circumstances force us to examine ourselves. **These adversities spur growth, creating needed change**. These transitions represent a next chapter in life, we must be ready to welcome that chapter, for there is no going back. Turn the page, keep reading the book, discover your story. I have seen patients transform from a career driven professional to an artist, or a stay at home grandparent. When they see and accept their new life, they love their new self.

> **[Graphic]** Slide "5) Healing mindset for healthy hormonal transitions": being hormonally challenged forces you to examine yourself, spurs growth, creates needed change, and is your next chapter. Image of rainbow butterfly wings with a saying that your time as a caterpillar is over and your wings are ready (third-party graphic).

This is the time for us to make those soul changes, especially when we are going through the pausal periods. **This is the time to appreciate our unique lives**, when we are caught on the hormonal roller coaster. Life will get better, but not perceptibly so, until we appreciate the change. **Any oncoming lows just means we have experienced a high, and the time will come when the low is done, and we experience the high again**. If we balance our hypothalamus, put healthy nutrition into our body, get the correct types of exercise our body needs to stay healthy, reboot our sleep, and have a healing mindset, than this transition will be an opportunity, not an obstacle. You can thrive during your hormonal transitions.

The beautiful display of Genesis Gold and Sacred Seven, to the left, demonstrates how you might feel, thriving during your hormonal transitions. Think “ may I thrive instead of just survive this hormonal transitions.”

> **[Graphic]** Closing slide "Thrive during hormonal transitions with Genesis Gold®" — www.genesisgold.com — with Genesis Gold and Sacred Seven surrounded by flowers, greens, herbs and powders.
