sections.title: Introduction
sections.text:
In this document, we will encourage you to Get Your Life Back, by becoming your own healer, as only you can do best. You will be learning how to heal yourself from the inside out, the outside in, and working through multiple aspects of healing that are arranged in five pillars. Let us first address how you will realize your vision for optimal health.

> **[Graphic]** Slide "What is your vision of optimal health?" — body, mind and soul — with a joyful woman leaping across a meadow holding streaming colored scarves.

What is your vision of optimal health? This vision about optimal health must be built around body, mind, and soul. If we cannot envision for ourselves where we want our health to go then it will be difficult to go there. If we hold in our mind’s eye our issues with weight, pain, or disease; then these fixations will be realized by the body. For instance, If we identify as a diabetic rather than our core identity, consider ourselves fat rather than fit, our body follows suit. **Having a clear vision about optimal health, unique to each person, is essential to that individual’s health**. Hold on to that vision as we explore it physically, mentally, and emotionally.

Imagine your Vision of health as a monumental iceberg, such as in the image to the Right. Our vision has outer aspects and inner aspects, hidden under the water of our self awareness. This iceberg model can apply to any goal, whether it is one’s physical health, love life or business. The portions of the vision above the water are the aspects of our vision that are perceptible in our personal environment. These environmental factors are the source of the most blame I hear patients place on their poor health; such as “I would be healthy if the rest of my family liked good food too”, or “I would be healthy if there wasn’t a street light outside my bedroom”. **We blame our environment, but we can also control our environment**, within limits, and we will focus on healthy ways of doing so later in this document. Your actions, both the behaviors you enact in habit and purposeful choices, contribute and are perceived by the outside world. We have some control here.

> **[Graphic]** Iceberg diagram of change: above the water are environment, actions and capabilities; below the surface, larger and deeper, are beliefs, values, identities and, at the base, vision. Lasting change starts from the deeper layers.

Your **capabilities** are stabilized at the level of the water. These are your strengths, exercised skills, education, and capacity to research and learn new capabilities. Some are good at research, others are quite organized, and some people are able to take part in active mindset training because they are very self aware. Then underneath the waterline lie your **beliefs** and these contribute to your subconscious voice. Our beliefs influence us on a deep level, and take time to change.

Also beneath the surface are those principles that you value. For instance, those who value fitness will find they make fitness part of their regular routine. Values can be quite concrete. But our values also encompass ideals such as honesty, truth, and the integrity to act on these values. These too affect our health. Our ideals do not only affect our business and relationships. Self awareness requires that we **investigate the difference between our values and our behavior**. Are we really being honest with ourselves, and are we really holding ourselves up to the highest level of integrity?

Lastly, who we believe ourselves to be influences our health because the depths of self contain our **identities**. I am not referring to categorical roles like being a mother, father, brother, sister, or a parent. I mean our identities as a person such as “I am a strong person”, or “I am a weak person”. What identities do you hold? Who do you believe yourself to be? How might your identities shape your vision about optimal health?

> **What is your Vision?**
> - Note down two environmental factors that shapes your behavior
> - List three of your beliefs
> - Examine two of your values
> - What is your strongest Identity?

> **[Graphic]** Slide "How to be your own health advocate": adapt your environment; schedule time for healthy actions; believe in yourself; partner with your health care provider; make healthy choices.

sections.title: How to Be Your Own Health Advocate
sections.text:
You are going to need to be your own health advocate. We cannot be our own healer, until we are comfortable advocating for ourselves. The strongest medium of self-advocacy is written in our surroundings, and so we must adapt our environment. You are going to adapt your own environment for your health and your optimal health needs. I recommend that you schedule time for healthy actions that will build your belief in yourself. I will now advise you to **partner with your healthcare provider**. I find that most people need a little bit of help, which is fine, but you are going to be the star and make your own healthier choices.

> **[Graphic]** Slide "Adapt your environment to match your vision": we are products of our conditioning, but you can reprogram yourself; when you change, your world shifts — change begins with you. Photo of hands holding the Earth.

**To change within, we will also change without**. Just as if we can change the inside of ourselves, then we can change the outer world too. As an example, I had a very elderly patient suffering from severe rheumatoid arthritis, and while she was quite handicapped by this she had been a very active woman. She loved spending much time with handicrafts, but her rheumatoid arthritis took all of that away from her. I found that her biggest issue during the healing process was that her spouse was unsupportive. She did not feel that he cared about her, and that he was unsupportive about whatever healing techniques she took. She even felt that she couldn’t speak about my care to her husband, as I was an integrative nurse practitioner, while he only believed in physicians and conventional medicine. So she felt her healing was unsupported by her spouse. After years of suffering through this, surviving on counseling, she finally realized that she had to change herself and she began to make a shift. She practiced mindset training and meditation to supplement her counseling. These things shifted the way she saw herself and her expectations of her husband. Without needing to verbalize these changes, she found that he began to be the supportive spouse. So as she shifted, he shifted into the person that she wished for. It happens every time, but **it starts with you**.

sections.title: Changing Yourself from Without
sections.text:
> **[Graphic]** Slide "Change within, change without" — a patient story: an elderly woman with arthritis and an unsupportive spouse, after years of suffering, realizes she must change herself; she shifts, and notices her husband begins to become the supportive spouse she always wished for.

It helps to adapt our environment to match our vision. We are a product of our conditioning, but you can reprogram yourself. For instance, many of us are conditioned to eat a certain way to clear our plate. “I put all that food on your plate, honey you better eat everything on your plate” is a message you may have heard while growing up. Messages like these create a conditioned response every time your plate is full to eat everything on your plate. But, **we can healthily reprogram that conditioned response**. How we do this is up to the individual, but the process is both gradual and works in degrees. As we change our environment we also change how we act to adapt to the environment, and thus we change our habits. This cascade of life changes begins with you! It begins with your shift in mindset and a shift in behaviors. We will explore this in more detail in the pages ahead.

> **[Graphic]** Slide "How to adapt your environment…": turn off lights at night; get the unhealthy food out of the house; set alarms to remind you to exercise, take a break and meditate; create a journey (vision) board and put it where you can see it; create a sacred space for meditation; journal regularly; find an unbiased accountability partner — not your spouse.

How do you adapt to your environment? We can train ourselves to healthier sleep, for instance, by turning off the lights at night. That means getting those cell phones, computers, anything with Wi-Fi built in, turned completely off and out of your bedroom. Next, turn off your lights, get that unhealthy food out of the house, and soon your whole life is different. After all, it is really hard to start a new nutritional program when you have a pantry full of junk food. The first time your diet causes you to feel weak you will be hungry, and you have yet to turn healthy ingredients into a healthy snack. You are going to see easy unhealthy snacks ready in that pantry, so dump it all. Get it all out of the house. If you have other family members or children who are not on your diet, why are you feeding them that junk anyway? It helps to clean up the house before you get started, and you can’t get started without setting alarm reminders to exercise, take a break, and to meditate. We will talk about those activities in more detail later. **Schedule changed behavior into your days** by letting alarms help us take breaks from the work that we are doing. We can also create a journey board or dream board and put it up where you can see it. More on these boards in a bit.

I also recommend creating a sacred space for **meditation** in your home or garden. If you have that space you will treat as sacred then you will take time to be there. You do not have to go to a church or temple to have a sacred moment. You can create that space within your own home. I recommend that my patients make use of a new journal regularly because writing down your insights on your health and life events can make a huge difference to self awareness. After all, looking back on your writing allows you to see your progress. It also helps to find an unbiased accountability partner that respects you but does not need to maintain peace through politeness. This is the reason it’s very difficult to partner with your spouse for accountability.

> **[Graphic]** Slide "Create a journey board": an example collage of images and words (water, nature, a swimmer, "strong," "in the flow," "balance," "thrive every day," "in motion," "dive in," "wild heart") — a visual board of the life and health you're moving toward.

So what does a **journey board** look like? To gain the benefits of such a board you will choose a blank poster board. Then cut meaningful pictures and words from many magazines to give form to your vision. Much like the model journey board, seen to the left, let us suppose a board was created toward obtaining optimal health. You would decorate your board with your vision for optimal health. You don’t need to cut out images of famous, skinny, fit people to put in the middle. That is their optimal health, and we want to focus on your vision of optimal health. Consider adding the places you would be able to go if your health improved. How would it feel to succeed? Would it feel like peace? Would it be exhilarating like a mountain climb? Would it be enjoyable as playing with grandchildren? Visualize and create what your goal would feel like. The journey or dream board is filled with images and words that represent where we want to go in terms of your optimal health vision. It is a very powerful way to focus, taking time to build this personal art, and then **having the board visible to help remind us of reaching this goal**. So if we take one thing from this section, let it be that starting a journey board is easy and effective. It is a great place to start for the next phase of your healing journey.

> **[Graphic]** Slide "Create a sacred space for you": examples — a curtained garden pavilion, a home altar corner for meditation, and a candlelit floor-cushion nook with a book.

How do we create **sacred space**? What does that look like? Depending on your location, you could find peace in an outdoor space, but indoor spaces work just as well. The space could have a religious altar-like feel to it, or it could just be a comfortable place to read, meditate, or pray. I am fortunate to have multiple sacred spaces around our property. I create altars on a regular basis, much like dream boards, they represent what I desire. I use special mementos that the altar holds. I also find it meaningful to create altars for others. We have a simple reserved alter out in our front yard made of rocks placed in a circle. This space is one of peacefulness because we have observed that space for peace. I find it very meditative while walking around that circle. Mazes and labyrinths can be meditative, and are made on holy grounds for that purpose. Your sacred space could be a quiet spot in your garden. It does not matter where the space is; only that you use it, reserve it only for this use, and tha**t you keep it sacred by keeping it tidy and reserved**. Utilize the sacredness you have created by taking time to be in that space, especially if you have a busy household. When I am in that space, I find the family just sort of leaves me alone for a moment.

> **Sacred Spaces:**
> - Sanctity is often a factor of separation from the mundane. How can you seperate your space?
> - Do you make peace by praying or reading? What books or deities would help most?
> - What would you depict on your vision/journey board?

sections.title: Find the Time to Discover a Healthier You
sections.text:
> **[Graphic]** Slide "Schedule time to be healthy": tasks fill the time you allot them, so schedule everything until it becomes habit — sleeping, exercising, eating, working, playing, meditating. "It takes 40 days to make a habit."

Consider the life you live now. When will you find time to do your meditation, your sacred reading, and work on your journey board? We all must find the time to make the effort, train your mind, and certainly to make your shifts. To do that, we all need to schedule time to be healthy. When time is scarce then we have to *make* time. Time seems to be limited when a person has so much to do from moment to moment that it can be difficult to look past that perspective of scarcity. I**f we do not schedule health into our day planner it is not going to happen**. We have to make it happen.

As a family nurse practitioner with a woman’s healthcare practice, I found effective strategies. I had multiple patients with kids coming to me pregnant, but no time to spend on their health. Some wanted to lose weight after their pregnancy, but could not find the time to make their health goals happen. How could I model it for them without being able to do this myself in my own busy family life? How could I explain to them how to make that time for health while exhausted by the end of the day if I could not answer that for myself? I learned that **we need to schedule health** by including better sleep, better exercise, better eating patterns, and plan it into our new life. By visualizing what that life is going to look like, making calculations and committing to keep that time, I found my own “me time” to stretch out. I found that tasks will fill the time you allot them.

So if you allow work to fill up all your time beyond a healthy 8 hour work schedule then you will not have any time to exercise and make other important changes in your life. Change will be much more effective if you carefully plan with realism and foresight. If you schedule all of those healthy behaviors into your day with one hour allotted for this task, half hour allotted for that task, two hours allotted for another task, and so on, then you will complete the tasks you planned to reach your goal. That is the way time works. Therefore, schedule *everything* until what you needed reminding to do becomes a habit. It usually takes 40 days for a person to make a habit. W**e may fail, and that is ok, as long as we keep going**. Keep scheduling, even if that means working on one thing at a time. Practice as it works best for you. If sleep is the biggest issue then focus on improving sleep habits for 40 days. If fitting exercise into the day is our biggest issue, then we work on our exercise plans until it becomes a habit.

> **[Graphic]** Slide "Put health on your day planner": a blank weekly planner (Sunday–Saturday, 7 a.m.–10 p.m.) for scheduling healthy activities.

So, we need to put health into your day planner. We need to fill out our schedules every day of the week and every half hour of the day. Prioritize sleep first and then we fit in health. We plan our waking and our sleeping, our work and our meditation breaks, our meals and our obligations. When will we exercise? We plan it and we do it. When will we have time for ourselves and time for our family? We plan that out too. Schedule everything and we make it happen.

sections.title: Focus on What You Can Do
sections.text:
How do we establish **a belief in ourselves** so we believe that we can actually heal? This is where mindset training comes in. Discovering what in your body resists this change is my prescribed first step. Where am I resistant in my mental space? Then uncover those limiting subconscious beliefs. We need to investigate everything keeping you from reaching your goals. Healing takes place by **tapping into our innate healer and tapping into our genetic potential**. I have mindset training that helps with this. There are many ways to tap into our genetic potential and make healing happen. It takes practice. This is not something that is going to happen overnight.

> **[Graphic]** Slide "Believe in yourself — mindset training helps": discover what in your body resists change; uncover limiting subconscious beliefs; tap into your innate healer; disentangle your cords of attachment; become your own "body whisperer"; and much more. Image of a head with a tree whose roots reach into the subconscious.

It is helpful to find someone else to be your **accountability partner** that does not live with you. If you are going to set a weight loss goal, a dietary goal, an exercise goal, or a healthy sleep goal it helps to have someone to report it to even if you communicate through social media. If you return the favor then you can become an accountability partner. Just having someone you can talk to can make all the difference. Knowing that **we have to report these changes to another person** will keep us honest. This helps us reach our goals faster and easier than being accountable only to yourself.

Disentangling your **cords of attachment** (not just to your parents as primary caretakers, but all your cords of attachment) can help you find your power. One of the activities I performed with the woman with rheumatoid arthritis was a disentanglement from her spouse. That exercise freed her up to do her own work. Working on this type of mindset training until the attempts become habit incorporate this into a meditation practice that will allow us to become our own **body whisperer**. We will start to be able to listen to our body without any entanglements and without any subconsciously held limiting beliefs which keep us from feeling a sense of empowerment. We will come to know what your body needs. So there are many ways to do this training. I just ask that you try it, and try making a habit of it.

sections.title: Self Sabotage
sections.text:
I would like to share with you a story about a woman who sabotaged herself. I had a patient that I had been counseling for years, and she constantly wanted to lose about 40 pounds. Her issue was that she would lose weight at first with diet and exercise. But then she would gain the weight right back again. Once I had [Genesis Gold](https://genesisgold.com/genesisgold/) available, she began taking it. Within the first six months of taking it, she realized that **she was limiting herself**. She had these limiting beliefs that would surface and she was compelled to make an empowerment shift.

> **[Graphic]** Slide "The woman who sabotaged herself" — a patient story: a woman sees her thinner self and her heavier self facing each other. She subconsciously linked "thin, sexy" with "unfaithful," and "heavy, stuck" with "safe." Deborah's account: after taking Genesis Gold, her limiting beliefs surfaced and she made an empowering shift.

We discovered that when she was actually heavier she felt as though her marriage was safe, because whenever she got thinner she felt conventionally sexier. She noticed she received more attention from other men, and she feared that she would be unfaithful. So she unconsciously released her diet and started gaining weight back again. She had no idea this was happening to her, and by her own hand. **She was not self aware until she started uncovering those limiting beliefs**. Once we worked on those limiting beliefs and she received counseling for herself and marital counseling for the both of them, she made an empowerment shift. She was able to lose that weight, feel good about herself, and feel safe in her marital relationship.

So looking at the ways **you might be sabotaging yourself,** perhaps through limiting beliefs in your subconscious, can really help. Believing in yourself that you can set your own goals and achieve your vision. We need to practice because what we practice is what we become. If you practice exercising every day, then exercise will become a part of you. If we practice healthy eating habits on a regular basis then healthy eating becomes us.

I recently went to a business conference where it was really hard to eat well. It is always hard to eat well when you are out and about, at a hotel, and eating with everyone else. I found myself choosing salads with some protein and looking for the vegetables with desperation. Especially when the conference tables were filled with Halloween candy and participants were chomping on candies just to keep their energy up through the boring presentations. Environments and circumstances can vastly change what healthy options are available.

sections.title: You Can Do It
sections.text:
> **[Graphic]** Slide "You can do it!": set your goals to achieve your vision; what you practice is what becomes. Photo of a rock climber scaling a cliff at sunset.

We are going to have to constantly be breaking bad habits in order to make healthy habits. Now this does not necessarily mean that we cannot take a break, but there is no excuse not to be healthy as the norm. **No matter where we are, we must get back up when we falter and keep at it**. Practice becomes habit. Ask ourselves, How can we eat out healthier? How can we make activity part of our lifestyle? How can we make meditation part of our lifestyle?

The next step, however, is **partnering with your healthcare provider**. Now this can be difficult because conventional medicine is slow to adapt. With no fault of the doctor, they eventually become guards to the status quo. Mine and older generations put those high level professions above everyone. Whatever the doctor said is treated as absolute truth, and patients are expected to do whatever the doctor said. This puts all the responsibility on the doctor and not on the patient. I have found that **when I partner with my patients they take responsibility for their behaviors**, and I hold them accountable as they hold me accountable. We work on accountability, and they achieve their health goals so much faster.

> **[Graphic]** Slide "Partner with your health care provider": choose a provider with similar health values; ask questions; do your homework; keep each other accountable — it's your body.

> **Do you Believe You can Do it?**
> - What ingrained beliefs could be holding you back?
> - What statements could you give to contradict these beliefs?
> - What beliefs do you have that you feel a doctor would judge you for?

To partner with your healthcare provider, we must first choose a healthcare provider. **Choose your general practitioner and specialists carefully**. They need to have similar health values as you and each other. If they absolutely disagree with your views on alternative medicine and you feel you must hide these practices from them, then there can be no healthy partnership. Find a Health Care Provider that will at least be open to hearing about what you are doing for yourself, and make appropriate recommendations. You do not want someone who will belittle your beliefs out of hand, but who will work with you.

You need to ask questions to your healthcare provider, and make a list before you go so you do not forget. Share these questions with them. **Do your homework**. There is nothing wrong with prior research, provided the sources are trustworthy. We healthcare providers actually expect you to do research. It is true that some healthcare providers get overwhelmed when patients bring in a large printed list of all their symptoms. You do not want to be left to diagnose yourself. A healthcare provider that is going to partner with you is going to consider your concerns and take them into account. Your self diagnosis may be wrong, but at least you have tried to do some research and are ready to work with them. This Philosophy keeps both parties accountable by being in a partnership together. By **committing to show up for appointments and keeping a daily log of details your doctor is concerned about tracking** are ways to show you are working to partner with your healthcare provider. You need them in order to reach your healthcare goals, but remember it is ultimately your body in question. Ultimately you decide everything you put into your body: medications, supplements, and even tests. Get a health care provider who respects your body autonomy and your personal health vision.

sections.title: Nutrition for Optimal Health
sections.text:
> **[Graphic]** Slide "2) Nutrition for optimal health": a variety of organic, in-season, locally grown colorful fruits and vegetables; enough healthy fats and adequate protein for your lean body mass; match carbs to your activity level; enough water for your body weight; limit processed foods.

While looking at nutrition for optimal health, we find that the Mediterranean based diet directs us to the healthiest variety of local in season organically grown colorful fruits and vegetables. Our produce must have a variety of **bright colors** to give us the largest variety of nutrients, not the bland and white standard American diet. We should not be eating a bland colorless white diet because it is not nutritious enough.

We also need sufficient healthy fats for our lean body mass. We need a half gram ( 0.50 g) of fat per pound of lean body mass. Healthy fats can be found in olive oil, coconut oil, nuts and seeds. Healthy fats are also in the good saturating fats found in fish and chicken. We need **adequate protein for our lean body mass, between half a gram and one gram (0.5–1 g) of protein per pound of lean body mass**. Our carbohydrate intake needs to be matched to our activity level. If we are sedentary, then we need much less carbs than a competitive athlete. If we are eating many carbs with every meal (such as breads, pastas, potato chips, and potatoes) and not burning them off then of course our body must store those carbs. Finally, we need enough water for our body weight. We need about one half ounce (.5oz) per pound of body weight. For instance, If you weigh 150 pounds then you need approximately seventy-five ounces of water.

> **[Graphic]** Slide "Learn how to read food labels": calories are not as important as protein, fat and actual carbs. Total carbs minus fiber = actual carbs. Example label: 40 g total carbohydrate − 4 g fiber = 36 g actual carbohydrates (the label also shows 250 calories, 6 g fat, 18 g sugars, 9 g protein per ¾-cup serving).

In order to control what we are putting in our mouth, we must learn how to read a food label. Please refer to the food label on the right. **It is preferable to eat whole food that does not need labels**; unprocessed meat, chicken, fish, and vegetables, but that is not easily possible, and marketers are required to label most foods.

Relative to current law, here is a tip on how to read the labels In those situations. Search out the portion labeled “nutrition facts” and look for the “serving size” because this data is key. The serving size in our image suggests a portion of three quarters of a cup (¾ cp). This indicates how much more Americans are eating than the nutritional suggested amounts and why so many of us can not lose that belly fat. I also suggest we pay attention to “serving size” because filling up the bowl does not mean we are only getting 250 calories from that particular food. Look to the “servings per container”, and then multiply that by
250. For our example, If you eat the whole package then you will have
had five times the serving size which means five times these listed calories, fat, cholesterol, sodium, total carbohydrates and protein. **Look to the number of calories per serving** and how many calories of that comes from fat, written here as a percentage.

> **Label Legend:**
> - Make a legend or key of common Nutritional Label terms to reference when reading labels
> - Note down quick calculations of how much protein, carbs, and fat you need per day
> - Check the labels against your notes

I advise you to *not* pay attention to the daily percentage values. Such calculations are always for a 2000 calorie per day diet. Instead, let us look at the actual grams. How many grams of fat are in that food? How many grams of protein are here? How many grams of carbohydrates? In our image with 250 calories, the majority is carbohydrates with some protein and a little fat. As you can see, calories are not as informative as the **portions** of protein, fat, and carbs. How do we determine the actual carbohydrates **per serving** in a food label? We take the total carbohydrates (in this case 40 gm) from which we subtract the dietary fiber (in this case four gm) and the remainder are the total carbohydrates (in this case 36 gm). According to this label, 18 gm of the total carbohydrates are sugars. The other half of these carbohydrates are starches. The only healthy carbohydrates in this label’s food are these four grams of fiber. The rest, the 36 grams, are the carbohydrates we have to count when we are limiting our carbohydrates per day. Pay attention to your sugar carbohydrates. Also remember the grams for each category amount are **per serving**.

sections.title: Physical Activity for Optimal Health
sections.text:
Now on to physical activity. So, remember that physical exercise is a three-legged stool. **In addition to aerobic, effective exercise includes stretching and weight resistance**. Weight resistance could be weight lifting but it could also be objects that use our own body weight, such as in a plank pulse, pushups, or pullups. Whether the weight is yours or external does not matter as long as you are balancing your exercise between the three “legs”. Aerobic exercise helps only when we get our heart rate up such as with dancing, running, swimming, bicycling, chasing children around the house, or jumping rope. Ensure that your h**eart rate is high enough that you cannot talk while exerting yourself**. Make sure to include flexibility activities such as stretching, yoga, or pilates. You can even use stretching bands, which can also be used as weight resistance. Our body needs all three.

> **[Graphic]** Slide "3) Physical activity for optimal health": weight resistance (resistance bands), aerobic exercise (treadmill), flexibility activities (lunging stretch).

How much aerobic activity should we do? We should be doing some type of aerobic activity three times a week in order to grow the healthiest heart, lungs, and ensure that our glucose metabolism is healthy. Additionally, we should be taking a long slow distance exercise once a week. As an LSD exercise passes about 30 minutes, a larger share of its energy comes from stored fat, and it also builds endurance. By contrast, **stretching and weight resistance exercise is necessary a couple of times a week.** Perhaps a yoga class that leads stretching and body weight resistance forms. For best results, conduct your own stretching on a daily basis.

> **[Graphic]** Table "Sample exercise schedule": Monday HIIT 20 minutes; Tuesday yoga 30 minutes; Wednesday HIIT with weight resistance 20 minutes; Thursday yoga 30 minutes; Friday HIIT 20 minutes; Saturday LSD (long slow distance) 2 hours; Sunday rest.

As mentioned before, new exercises do not get done without a schedule. Let us look at the sample exercise schedule above as a guide to make our own. On Monday, twenty minutes are assigned to HIT exercise, which includes some preliminary stretching. On Tuesday, we are going to do yoga. I prefer yoga, while others may use pilates, to the same benefit of weight and flexibility. Because HIT exercise includes flexibility as well, I like to balance that activity with something requiring weight resistance. Doing a fitness park body-weight utilizing a circuit could serve this purpose. These circuits can be found in gyms and the yards of local schools. Taking a brisk walk to a handy fence post for push ups could serve just as well. I recommend **three rounds of a single movement repeated ten times**. You may notice this pattern also is found in a HIT routine. For both cases, I recommend a two minute fast walk in between these three rounds of repetitions. Tricep dips against a chair would make an excellent body weight resistance repetition. Or, we could scooch our bottom off that chair, dip down and use our arm strength to lift our body. The specific exercise is not important, as long as you are moving your body weight around.

> **An Exercise in Note taking:**
> - Take a weekly journal of your exercise habits and write down every strenuous/enduring activity
> - Compare your results against the requirements above
> - Have you blocked out four hours a week for exercise? Make your Schedule!

Please note how much time we have allotted here. So far we have only detailed two hours in these five days. To add a single **long slow distance**, is an additional two hours, in a single block. An LSD could be a hike, maybe ending with a picnic to enjoy with loved ones! Just get out and move, whether it be walking a circuit around the mall for two hours, just keep moving. If you live in a cold winter, there is no reason not to hold your LSD indoors. But do make sure you rest, one day a week. This schedule is just a sample. You can plan your exercises you need, but you have got to schedule it.

sections.title: Sleep for Optimal Health
sections.text:
> **[Graphic]** Slide "4) Sleep for optimal health": sleep in the dark; wake up with the sun.

Sleeping is essential for optimal health. Remember to remove all wireless devices and electronic lights, blue tinted especially, out of your bedroom and sleep in the dark. With all of the lights off, all of the digital lights covered, we can enjoy uninterrupted sleep. These electronic stimulants interrupt our melatonin production which cause flux prolactin during the day. This results in autoimmunity, a depression in your metabolism and weight gain. I recommend you try to wake up with natural sunlight. If you are not able to do that, perhaps because of your bedroom’s location or the need for blackout curtains, I recommend you get an alarm that projects natural light as it wakes you up. **We should stand in natural sunlight for at least twenty minutes everyday,** especially in the morning. This is the most important time for switching off melatonin and boosting serotonin to aid our brain chemistry. We will be happier and more focused with a daily dose of vitamin D created by sunlight.

sections.title: Healing Mindset for Optimal Health
sections.text:
> **[Graphic]** Slide "5) Healing mindset for optimal health": shift toward empowering beliefs; acknowledge your deepest values; know who you are; have a clear vision of the optimally healthy you. Artwork of a serene blue-skinned woman resting her head on her hand.

What is a healing mindset for optimal health? We need to shift towards more **empowering beliefs**. It helps to not say “can’t” anymore, we can shift to “I can” affirmations. When I was a young girl, I remember my dad would scold me if I used the word “can’t”, and that may have helped me. There is no “can’t”, there is only “I can” or “I will try”. But no “can’t”. There is nothing you cannot do, you can do anything. We need to shift our beliefs so that they are moving toward empowering our agency. **We need to talk to our body in a positive way**, and we need to encourage the body as it is our home. I remember a patient with severe osteoporosis, and she would complain about how weak she was every time she got on the phone with me. So I said, “As long as you keep using those words your bones are going to keep disintegrating.''

> **[Graphic]** Slide "Become your own body whisperer with Genesis Gold": a jar of Genesis Gold over a DNA double helix.

I recommend we start talking about ourselves as if we are each a strong empowered person until we believe it then our body will fit our beliefs. By acknowledging our deepest values it allows us to see what beliefs we have that do not value health, and then make the shift away from those beliefs. Know who you are, know what your truth is, and know what makes you the happiest. I suggest you play to your strengths, start working on what you consider to be your weaknesses, and transform them in to your powers. We must have a really clear vision of what optimal health looks like, and more so what optimal health **feels** like. “I have energy. I feel peace. I have joy.” Optimal health is not just about looking great, it is about feeling great.
